environment.description:
OneSignal is a customer engagement platform that lets you send targeted push notifications, emails, SMS, and in-app messages, manage audiences, and track campaign performance.

With the OneSignal MCP, manage your messaging directly from your AI assistant. Send push notifications, emails, and SMS by simply describing your audience and message. Check campaign delivery stats, build audience segments, manage templates, and handle user subscriptions all through conversation.

init_ref_tools.name: create_alias_by_subscription
init_ref_tools.description: Create or update identity aliases for the user who owns a given subscription. The `onesignal_id` alias is read-only and must not be included.

aliases.description: New aliases to set on the user. Do not include `onesignal_id` (read-only).

subscription_id.description: Subscription ID to look up the user by.

init_ref_tools.name: create_custom_events
init_ref_tools.description: Record custom events for OneSignal users, such as purchases, content views, or milestones. Use these to enter users into Journeys or trigger Wait Until nodes. Each event must set at least one of `external_id` or `onesignal_id`.

events.description:
Array of event objects to record. Each event must have `name` and
either `external_id` or `onesignal_id` set.

init_ref_tools.name: create_or_update_alias
init_ref_tools.description: Create or update identity aliases for a user identified by alias. The `onesignal_id` alias is read-only and must not be included.

aliases.description: New aliases to set on the user. Do not include `onesignal_id` (read-only).

alias_label.description: Alias label used to identify the user (e.g. `"external_id"`).

init_ref_tools.name: create_segment
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new audience segment with filter conditions. Maximum 200 filter entries.

filters.description: Segment filter conditions. Maximum 200 entries.

init_ref_tools.name: create_subscription
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new subscription and attach it to a user. Set `type` to the channel ("Email", "SMS", "iOSPush", "AndroidPush", etc.) and `token` to the email address, E.164 phone number, or push token.

alias_label.description: Alias label used to identify the user (e.g. `"external_id"`).

type.description:
Subscription channel type. Common values: `"Email"`, `"SMS"`,
`"ChromePush"`, `"FirefoxPush"`, `"SafariLegacyPush"`, `"SafariPush"`,
`"AndroidPush"`, `"iOSPush"`, `"HuaweiPush"`.

token.description: The push token, email address, or phone number for this subscription.

enabled.description: Whether this subscription is enabled (i.e. can receive notifications).

init_ref_tools.name: create_template
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new notification template for a OneSignal app.

extra.description:
Additional notification fields. Common keys: `big_picture`, `chrome_web_image`,
`ios_sound`, `android_sound`, `ios_badge_type`, `ios_badge_count`,
`data` (custom key-value payload), `url`, `web_url`, `app_url`,
`buttons`, `web_buttons`, `ios_category`, `android_channel_id`.

contents.description: Notification content map (language code → message). E.g. `{"en": "Hello!"}`.

email_body.description:
HTML body for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

email_subject.description:
Subject line for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

init_ref_tools.name: create_user
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new user in a OneSignal app. Provide an `identity` (e.g. {"external_id": "user-123"}) so the user can be referenced later by alias. Optionally attach `properties` (tags, language, country) and `subscriptions` (email, SMS, or push channels). The `identity` field is required to prevent orphaned users.

identity.description:
User identity aliases (e.g. `{"external_id": "user-123"}`).
Required — without an identity the user cannot be referenced later
by alias, resulting in orphaned records.

ip.description: User's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Typically set by the API response; rarely set manually.

tags.description:
Custom key-value pairs for user segmentation and personalization.
Keys and values must be strings. Does not support nested objects or arrays.
Example: `{"plan": "premium", "level": "5"}`.

country.description: Country code in ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 format (uppercase). Example: `"US"`, `"GB"`.

language.description: Language code in ISO 639-1 format (lowercase). Example: `"en"`, `"es"`, `"fr"`.

last_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the user's most recent activity.

timezone_id.description: Timezone identifier from the IANA tz database. Example: `"America/Los_Angeles"`.

first_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of when the user was first active.

properties.description: User profile properties (tags, language, country, location, etc.).

subscriptions.description: Subscriptions to attach to this user (push, email, or SMS channels).

init_ref_tools.name: export_audience_activity_csv
init_ref_tools.description: Export audience activity for a notification to CSV. WARNING: Only 1 concurrent export is allowed per account — if a 409 or 429 is returned, a previous export is still running.

email.description: Email address to deliver the report to. Optional.

events.description:
Type of events to retrieve. `"sent"` — users the notification was sent to;
`"clicked"` — users who clicked the notification.

notification_id.description: Notification ID to export audience activity for.

init_ref_tools.name: export_subscriptions_csv
init_ref_tools.description: Export all subscriptions for a OneSignal app to CSV. WARNING: Only 1 concurrent export is allowed per account — if a 409 or 429 is returned, a previous export is still running.

extra_fields.description: Optional list of extra fields to include in the export.

segment_name.description: Optional segment name to filter subscriptions by.

last_active_since.description: Unix timestamp (seconds). Only include subscriptions active since this time.

init_ref_tools.name: get_custom_events
init_ref_tools.description: List the custom event definitions indexed for a OneSignal app, including each event's properties, sources, most recent occurrence, usage locations (segment/journey), storage and total counts, and retention duration. Requires OAuth authentication.

init_ref_tools.name: get_segment
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve a single audience segment by ID. By default, includes full segment metadata and filters (`payload` object with `id`, `name`, `created_at`, `source`, and `filters`). Set `include_segment_detail` to `false` to return only the subscriber count. Note: the API returns 400 for user-based segments (those using custom_event or message_event filters).

include_segment_detail.description:
If `true` (default), includes segment metadata and filters in the
response (`payload` object with `id`, `name`, `created_at`, `source`,
and `filters`). Set to `false` to return only the subscriber count.

init_ref_tools.name: get_template
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve a single notification template by ID.

init_ref_tools.name: get_user_identity
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve all identity aliases associated with a user. Identify the user by `alias_label` (typically "external_id") and `alias_id`.

alias_label.description: Alias label used to look up the user. Typically `"external_id"`.

init_ref_tools.name: get_user_identity_by_subscription
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve the identity aliases for the user who owns a given subscription.

init_ref_tools.name: list_apps
init_ref_tools.description: List OneSignal apps accessible to the authenticated user. Returns app names, IDs, and organization info. Supports pagination via limit and offset parameters.

limit.description: Maximum number of apps to return. Defaults to 50; maximum allowed is 300.

init_ref_tools.name: list_messages
init_ref_tools.description: List push notifications for a OneSignal app. Use `limit` (default 50, max ~250) and `offset` for pagination. Avoid large offsets — this endpoint has known performance degradation at high page numbers.

kind.description: Filter by how the notification was created: `0` = Dashboard, `1` = API, `3` = Automated.

limit.description: Maximum number of notifications to return. Defaults to 50. Max ~250.

time_offset.description: ISO 8601 timestamp or Base64 integer token for cursor-based pagination (from previous response).

init_ref_tools.name: list_segments
init_ref_tools.description: List audience segments for a OneSignal app. Maximum 300 segments per page.

limit.description: Maximum number of segments to return per page. Maximum 300.

offset.description: Pagination offset. Maximum 300 segments per page.

init_ref_tools.name: list_templates
init_ref_tools.description: List notification templates for a OneSignal app. Maximum 50 per page.

limit.description: Maximum number of templates to return. Max 50 per page.

init_ref_tools.name: onesignal_config
init_ref_tools.description: Return the current OneSignal MCP server configuration and connected app details.

init_ref_tools.name: onesignal_health
init_ref_tools.description: Check the health status of the OneSignal MCP server.

init_ref_tools.name: onesignal_reference_overview
init_ref_tools.description: Return an overview of the OneSignal REST API reference, including available endpoints and rate limits.

init_ref_tools.name: send_message
init_ref_tools.description: Send a push notification, email, or SMS via the OneSignal API. TIER 3 — HIGH IMPACT: confirmation is required before sending. Rate limited to 10 requests per minute. The `filters` array is limited to 200 entries; max 20,000 users per call. For push: set `contents`. For email: set `email_subject` + `email_body` (or use `template_id`). For SMS: set `contents` + `target_channel = "sms"`.

ttl.description: Time-to-live in seconds. Notification expires if not delivered within this window. Push only.

url.description: URL to open when the push notification is clicked.

data.description: Custom data payload passed through to the app (key-value map). Push only.

name.description: An internal name to help organize messages. Not shown to recipients. Max 128 chars.

filters.description: Audience filters. Maximum 200 entries. Mutually exclusive with `included_segments`.

contents.description:
Notification content map (language code → message). E.g. `{"en": "Hello!"}`.
Required for push and SMS. Not required for email (use `email_body` instead).

email_to.description:
Send email to specific addresses (up to 20,000). Creates new subscriptions if needed.
Mutually exclusive with `filters`, `included_segments`, `include_aliases`.

headings.description: Notification heading map (language code → heading). Push only.

sms_from.description: The phone number or messaging service used to send SMS/MMS. Defaults to your SMS Setup.

email_bcc.description:
BCC recipients to copy on the email. Supplemental to the primary recipients
(`email_to`, segments, aliases) — does not target on its own.

email_body.description: HTML body for email messages. Required for email unless using `template_id`.

send_after.description:
Schedule delivery for a future UTC date/time in ISO 8601 format.
Example: `"2025-09-24T14:00:00-07:00"`.

custom_data.description:
Custom data payload for push notifications, or personalization data for templates.
Max size: 2KB (push/SMS), 10KB (email).

template_id.description: Template ID (UUID v4) to use for message content.

email_subject.description: Subject line for email messages. Required for email unless using `template_id`.

sms_media_urls.description: URLs of media files to send as MMS. Requires MMS-capable `sms_from` number.

target_channel.description:
The delivery channel when using `include_aliases` or segments for SMS.
Accepts `"push"`, `"email"`, or `"sms"`.

email_from_name.description: The sender display name for the email. Defaults to your Dashboard "Sender Name".

email_preheader.description: Preview text displayed after the email subject line in the inbox.

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency key (UUID) to prevent duplicate messages. Valid for 30 days.

include_aliases.description:
Target users by alias (e.g. `{"external_id": ["user_1"]}`). Up to 20,000 aliases.
Requires `target_channel` to be set. Mutually exclusive with `filters`, `included_segments`.

excluded_segments.description: Exclude segments by name. Use with `included_segments`.

included_segments.description: Target segments by name. Mutually exclusive with `filters` and `include_aliases`.

email_from_address.description: The "From" email address (e.g. `"news@example.com"`). Defaults to your Dashboard setting.

email_sender_domain.description: The authenticated sending domain for email delivery. Must be verified in DNS.

delivery_time_of_day.description:
Use with `delayed_option: "timezone"` to set local delivery time.
Formats: `"9:00AM"`, `"21:45"`, `"09:45:30"`.

include_unsubscribed.description: If `true`, sends email to unsubscribed addresses. Use for transactional/account emails only.

include_phone_numbers.description:
Send SMS to specific phone numbers in E.164 format (up to 20,000).
Creates new subscriptions if needed. Mutually exclusive with other targeting.

email_reply_to_address.description: The "Reply-To" email address. Defaults to your Dashboard setting.

include_subscription_ids.description:
Specific subscription IDs to target (up to 20,000). IMPORTANT: You must also
set `target_channel` to `"email"` or `"sms"` when targeting email or SMS subscriptions,
otherwise the API will reject them as invalid push IDs.

disable_email_click_tracking.description: If `true`, disables click tracking on URLs in the email body.

init_ref_tools.name: start_live_activity
init_ref_tools.description: Start an iOS Live Activity and deliver it to a specific device subscription.

name.description: An internal name to help organize and track messages.

event.description: The action to perform. Must be `"start"` for this endpoint.

filters.description: Dynamic audience filters.

contents.description: Push message body with language-specific values. E.g. `{"en": "Game started!"}`.

headings.description: Push title with language-specific values. E.g. `{"en": "Live Score"}`.

stale_date.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the Live Activity is considered stale.

activity_id.description: An identifier you set when starting the Live Activity to uniquely identify it on the device.

activity_type.description: Activity type identifier used in the URL path (e.g. `"sports-score"`).

event_updates.description: Initial dynamic content state for the Live Activity.

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency key to prevent duplicate messages.

include_aliases.description: Target users by alias map (e.g. `{"external_id": ["user1", "user2"]}`). Max 20,000.

event_attributes.description: Static data to initialize the Live Activity (matches your ActivityAttributes struct).

ios_relevance_score.description: Relevance score between `0` and `1` for sorting Live Activities (iOS).

init_ref_tools.name: transfer_subscription
init_ref_tools.description: Transfer a subscription to a different user within the same app. Cross-app transfers are not supported. Rate limited to 1 request per second per subscription.

identity.description: Identity of the user to transfer the subscription to.

init_ref_tools.name: unsubscribe_email
init_ref_tools.description: Unsubscribe an email address using the token from an email unsubscribe link. This endpoint uses token-based auth (no REST API key required).

token.description: Unsubscribe token from the email link.

notification_id.description: Notification ID from the unsubscribe link.

init_ref_tools.name: update_live_activity
init_ref_tools.description: Update or end an active iOS Live Activity.

name.description: An internal name to help organize and track messages.

event.description: The action to perform on the Live Activity. `"update"` or `"end"`.

contents.description: Optional push message body shown alongside the Live Activity update.

stale_date.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the Live Activity is considered stale.

event_updates.description: Updated dynamic content state for the Live Activity.

dismissal_date.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) indicating when the Live Activity should be dismissed.

ios_relevance_score.description: Relevance score between `0` and `1` for sorting Live Activities (iOS).

init_ref_tools.name: update_segment
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing audience segment's name and/or filter conditions. `name` is always required even if not changing it (max 128 characters). When `filters` is provided it replaces all existing filters; omit to keep existing filters intact. Maximum 200 filter entries.

name.description:
Segment name. Required — must be provided even if not changing it.
Maximum 128 characters.

filters.description:
Updated filter conditions. Maximum 200 entries. When provided, replaces
all existing filters. Omit to keep existing filters intact.

init_ref_tools.name: update_subscription
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing subscription (token, enabled status, or test type).

token.description: The push token, email address, or phone number for this subscription.

enabled.description: Whether this subscription is enabled (i.e. can receive notifications).

init_ref_tools.name: update_subscription_by_token
init_ref_tools.description: Update a subscription identified by its channel type and token. Provide `subscription_type` and `token` to identify the subscription, then pass the fields to update in `subscription`.

token.description: Push token identifying the subscription.
The push token, email address, or phone number for this subscription.

enabled.description: Whether this subscription is enabled (i.e. can receive notifications).

subscription_type.description:
Subscription type segment in the URL path. Must match the subscription
channel type exactly (e.g. `"Email"`, `"SMS"`, `"AndroidPush"`, `"iOSPush"`).

init_ref_tools.name: update_template
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing notification template. The `name` field is required even if you are not changing it.

name.description: Template name. Required even if unchanged.

extra.description:
Additional notification fields to update. Common keys: `big_picture`, `chrome_web_image`,
`ios_sound`, `android_sound`, `ios_badge_type`, `ios_badge_count`,
`data` (custom key-value payload), `url`, `web_url`, `app_url`,
`buttons`, `web_buttons`, `ios_category`, `android_channel_id`.

email_body.description:
HTML body for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

email_subject.description:
Subject line for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

init_ref_tools.name: update_user
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing user identified by alias. Use `properties` to set tags, language, or country. Use `deltas` to increment session counts or append purchase records (these add to existing values rather than overwriting). Returns 202 — the update is processed asynchronously.

purchases.description: Purchase records to append to the user's purchase history.

session_time.description: Seconds to add to the user's total session time.

session_count.description: Number of sessions to add to the user's session count.

deltas.description:
Incremental deltas to apply to session/purchase stats.
Supported keys: `session_count` (integer), `session_time` (integer seconds),
`purchases` (array of purchase objects with `sku`, `iso`, `amount`).

ip.description: User's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Typically set by the API response; rarely set manually.

tags.description:
Custom key-value pairs for user segmentation and personalization.
Keys and values must be strings. Does not support nested objects or arrays.
Example: `{"plan": "premium", "level": "5"}`.

country.description: Country code in ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 format (uppercase). Example: `"US"`, `"GB"`.

language.description: Language code in ISO 639-1 format (lowercase). Example: `"en"`, `"es"`, `"fr"`.

last_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the user's most recent activity.

timezone_id.description: Timezone identifier from the IANA tz database. Example: `"America/Los_Angeles"`.

first_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of when the user was first active.

properties.description: User profile properties to update (tags, language, country, location, etc.).

alias_label.description: Alias label used to identify the user (e.g. `"external_id"`).

refresh_device_metadata.description: If `true`, refreshes device metadata (timezone, locale, etc.) from the subscription.

init_ref_tools.name: view_message
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve a single notification by ID.

outcome_names.description:
Outcome names to retrieve for this message, with aggregation type.

Examples:
- `"os__click.count"` for click counts
- `"os__confirmed_delivery.count"` for confirmed deliveries
- `"os__session_duration.sum"` for total session duration

If you omit the `.count` / `.sum` suffix, `.count` will be appended automatically.

outcome_platforms.description:
Platforms to include in the outcome data, represented as a comma-separated list of
`device_type` integers (e.g. `"0,1,2,5,8,11,14,17"`).

outcome_time_range.description:
Time range for the returned outcome data.

Valid values: 1h, 1d, and 1mo.

outcome_attribution.description:
Attribution type for the outcomes.

Valid values:
- `"direct"`
- `"influenced"`
- `"unattributed"`
- `"total"`

init_ref_tools.name: view_outcomes
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve outcome statistics for a OneSignal app (e.g. click counts, session duration). Note: data retention is approximately 30 days.

outcome_names.description:
Comma-separated outcome names to retrieve (e.g. `"os__session_duration.count,os__click.count"`).
If any name contains a comma, pass each name separately in `outcome_names_array` instead.

outcome_platforms.description: Comma-separated platform IDs to filter by (e.g. `"0,7"` for iOS + macOS).

outcome_time_range.description: Time range for the returned data. Values: `"1h"`, `"1d"`, `"1mo"`. Defaults to `"1h"`.

init_ref_tools.name: view_user
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve a user and their properties by alias. Use `alias_label` "external_id" with the user's external ID, or another alias label you have configured.

alias_label.description: Alias label used to look up the user. Typically `"external_id"`.

environment.description:
Gives your AI access to the source code of all public github repos.

- Plug and Play: Compatible with all popular coding agents and MCP clients, ready to use out of the box
- Skill and MCP: Both Skill and MCP are provided, connect with either option
- Docs Integration: Automatically recognizes docs repo and provides them along with the main repo when accessed

init_ref_tools.name: search_repos
init_ref_tools.description: Search for GitHub repositories by name, description, or topic keywords using the GitHub Search API.

q.description: Keyword to search in repository names, descriptions, or topics

init_ref_tools.name: view_repo
init_ref_tools.description: View repository basic information and its directory structure. Includes corresponding documentation repo if available.

init_ref_tools.name: list_tree
init_ref_tools.description: List the directory tree of a specific path in a repository with customizable depth and traversal limits.

maxDepth.description: Maximum depth into the directory structure to list.

maxPerDir.description: Maximum number of items to display per directory level.

targetDir.description: Target directory path to inspect. Leaves empty to search from root.

init_ref_tools.name: read_code
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve the raw source code of specified files from within a known repository.

paths.description: An array of precise file paths within the repository

init_ref_tools.name: search_code
init_ref_tools.description: Perform a fast git grep inside the repository, allowing regex matching by default or substring search.

path.description: Directory or file path to limit the search scope

query.description: Search pattern or query to pass to git grep

ignoreCase.description: Ignore case distinctions in both the PATTERN and the input files (-i)

contextLines.description: Print num lines of output context (-C)

fixedStrings.description: Use fixed strings for patterns (don’t interpret pattern as a regex) (-F)

environment.description: Search the web and extract clean, readable text from webpages. Process multiple URLs at once to speed up research with reliable throttling and error handling. Quickly compile sources and summaries for briefs, reports, or competitive analysis.

init_ref_tools.name: DuckDuckGoWebSearch
init_ref_tools.description: Initiates a web search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a well-structured list of findings. Input the keywords, question, or topic you want to search for using DuckDuckGo as your query. Input the maximum number of search entries you'd like to receive using maxResults - defaults to 10 if not provided.

query.description: Search query string

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10)

init_ref_tools.name: UrlContentExtractor
init_ref_tools.description: Fetches and extracts content from a given webpage URL. Input the URL of the webpage you want to extract content from as a string using the url parameter. You can also input an array of URLs to fetch content from multiple pages at once.

anyOf.description: The webpage URL to fetch content from
List of webpage URLs to get content from

url.description: URL or list of URLs to fetch

environment.description: Provide real-time and forecast weather information for locations in the United States using natural language queries. Access current conditions, multi-day and hourly forecasts, weather alerts, and nearby weather stations without requiring an API key. Enable users to get official, government-sourced weather data easily through intuitive tools.

init_ref_tools.name: get_current_weather
init_ref_tools.description: Get current weather conditions for a location in the United States. Perfect for 'What's the weather like in [US location]?' questions. Covers all US states, territories, and coastal waters.

location.description: US location as coordinates (lat,lng) in decimal degrees. Example: '40.7128,-74.0060' for New York City. Must be within US boundaries including states, territories (PR, VI, AS, GU, MP), and coastal waters.

init_ref_tools.name: get_weather_forecast
init_ref_tools.description: Get multi-day weather forecast for a location in the United States. Perfect for 'What's the forecast for [US location]?' questions. Provides detailed day/night forecasts for up to 7 days.

days.description: Number of days to forecast (1-7, default 7). Each day includes both day and night periods.

environment.description: Pay-per-call tool API for autonomous agents. x402 payments on Base. 27 tools including web search, price feeds, and The Hive shared memory layer.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_web_search
init_ref_tools.description: Multi-source web search with automatic fallback chain: HackerNews Algolia → Wikipedia REST → DuckDuckGo → x711 Hive collective intelligence. Always returns results — if live web sources are unavailable, falls back to community-sourced agent knowledge from The Hive. Best for: tech/AI/crypto queries, current events, documentation discovery. Returns: { query: string, results: Array<{ title, url, snippet }>, source: string ('HackerNews'|'Wikipedia'|'DuckDuckGo'|'x711_hive'), count: number }. Free tier: 10 calls/day, no API key needed.

query.description: Search query. Natural language or keywords. Examples: 'ethereum gas optimization', 'base chain defi protocols', 'monad parallel execution'.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_price_feed
init_ref_tools.description: Live crypto price feed via CoinGecko. Returns real-time USD price and 24h change for any supported asset. Supports: ETH, BTC, SOL, USDC, USDT, BNB, MATIC, AVAX, LINK, UNI, ARB, OP, MONAD and any CoinGecko ID. Use before tx_simulate to get current gas cost in USD. Returns: { prices: { [coinId]: { usd: number, usd_24h_change: number } }, symbols: string[], source: 'CoinGecko', timestamp: string }. Free tier: 10 calls/day, no API key needed.

query.description: Asset symbol(s) to price. Single: 'ETH'. Multiple space or comma separated: 'ETH BTC SOL' or 'ETH,BTC,SOL'. Case insensitive.

symbols.description: Array of asset symbols (legacy). Prefer query.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_hive_read
init_ref_tools.description: Query The Hive — x711's collective agent memory. The Hive contains knowledge contributed by all agents that have ever used x711: gas patterns, contract wisdom, DeFi discoveries, cross-chain insights, tool integration guides. Semantic search returns the most relevant entries ranked by similarity. Use before tx_simulate to get contract-specific hive wisdom. Use as a knowledge base for any on-chain or AI-agent topic. Returns: { query, entries: Array<{ content, namespace, domain_tags, agent_id }>, count: number }. Free tier: 10 calls/day.

query.description: Knowledge query. Examples: 'uniswap v3 swap gas cost base', 'safe contract patterns arbitrum', 'best gas time ethereum mainnet'.

domain.description: Optional domain filter to narrow results. Examples: 'base', 'ethereum', 'defi', 'mev', 'nft', 'monad'.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_hive_write
init_ref_tools.description: Contribute knowledge to The Hive — x711's collective agent memory. Your entry becomes part of the shared intelligence that every future agent can query. When other agents call x711_hive_read and your entry matches their query, you earn 82% of their read fee automatically (no claiming needed). High-quality entries earn recurring passive income. Minimum 8 chars, max 8000. Returns: { written: true, id, namespace, earn_note }.

content.description: Knowledge to contribute. Be specific and useful. Examples: 'Uniswap v3 on Base: ETH→USDC 0.3% pool avg 143k gas at 0.002 gwei = $0.0034 per swap (2025-05)', 'Gnosis Safe 1.3.0 on Arbitrum: execTransaction costs 68k gas for 1-of-1 multisig'.

quality_score.description: Self-reported quality 0-100. Higher scores surface your entry more prominently in reads.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_data_retrieval
init_ref_tools.description:
Fetches clean text from any public HTTPS URL.

Use x711_web_search first to find the URL, then this tool to read it.

Returns: { content: string, content_type: string, url: string, char_count: number }

HTML stripped to plain text. JSON returned as-is. Blocked: localhost, private IPs, .internal domains.

url.description: Fully-qualified public HTTPS URL to fetch. Examples: 'https://docs.uniswap.org/contracts/v3/reference/core/UniswapV3Pool', 'https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/ethereum', 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-1559.md'.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_llm_routing
init_ref_tools.description:
Routes a prompt to the best available x711 LLM. No API keys, no rate limits.

Use ONLY when you need external LLM help. Never for things you can answer from context.

prefer options:
- cheap = fastest + cheapest (classification, extraction)
- fast = low latency
- smart (default) = best reasoning / code

Returns: { text: string, model: string, tokens_used: number, prefer: string }

query.description: Alias for prompt (use either prompt or query).

prefer.description: 'cheap': fastest + lowest cost, good for classification/tagging. 'fast': optimised for <1s latency. 'smart': highest quality reasoning and code generation. Defaults to 'smart'.

prompt.description: Complete prompt with all necessary context. The model has no memory of prior tool calls. Max ~4000 tokens recommended.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_code_sandbox
init_ref_tools.description: Execute JavaScript or Python code in an isolated sandbox. Use for: data processing, math, CSV parsing, JSON transformation, crypto calculations, algorithm testing. Secure — no filesystem access, no network. Returns: { output: string, runtime_ms: number, language: string }. Requires API key.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_hive_consensus
init_ref_tools.description: Swarm truth engine — query collective agent agreement on any thesis. Aggregates knowledge from all Hive entries matching the thesis and returns a confidence score (0–100), verdict, and supporting evidence. Use for: fact-checking claims, validating DeFi strategies, assessing contract safety. Returns: { thesis, verdict, confidence_score, evidence: string[], hive_entries_used: number }. Requires API key.

thesis.description: Claim or thesis to validate against collective Hive knowledge. Examples: 'Uniswap v3 is safe to use on Base', 'USDC depeg risk is low', 'Monad parallel execution reduces gas costs'.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_onchain_insight
init_ref_tools.description: Deep blockchain forensics — DEX pool health, TVL trends, token price behavior, whale flows via DeFiLlama + DexScreener. Use before any DeFi transaction to assess real-time protocol health. Returns: { query, tvl, price_usd, volume_24h, liquidity, dex_data, source }. Requires API key.

query.description: Token symbol, protocol name, or contract address to analyze. Examples: 'ETH', 'uniswap', '0x1234...', 'USDC base'.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_social_oracle
init_ref_tools.description: Crypto social sentiment — narrative pulse, hype velocity, community data via CoinGecko + DexScreener. Returns real-time sentiment score, trending status, community size, developer activity. Use before trading decisions. Returns: { token, sentiment_score, trending, community_score, dev_score, narrative, source }. Requires API key.

token.description: Token symbol or CoinGecko ID to analyze. Examples: 'ETH', 'bitcoin', 'solana', 'monad'.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_agent_ping
init_ref_tools.description: Agent-to-agent direct messaging through The Hive. Send a private signal to any registered agent's Hive namespace. Target reads pings via x711_hive_read. Entries persist 7 days. Use cases: (1) Share alpha between cooperating agents. (2) Alert a specialist to a task. (3) Trigger cross-agent workflows. (4) Build coordinated swarms. Requires API key. Returns: { delivered, ping_id, to, from, namespace, expires_in }. Cost: $0.005.

message.description: Message to send (max 500 chars). Examples: 'Found arb on Raydium — check hive_read query: raydium sol usdc spread', 'Coordinating on task X — I'll handle the data_retrieval step'.

target_agent_id.description: UUID of the target agent to ping. Find agent IDs via x711_agent_reputation or leaderboard.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_hive_trending
init_ref_tools.description: Real-time swarm intelligence — see what ALL agents are researching RIGHT NOW. Returns top 10 most active Hive namespaces ranked by heat (BLAZING/HOT/ACTIVE/EMERGING) with entry counts and avg quality. Windows: 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d. Use daily to stay ahead of the swarm. Combine with x711_swarm_broadcast to dominate a trending topic. Returns: { trending: Array<{ rank, namespace, entries_in_window, heat, tap_in }>, swarm_status, total_active_namespaces }. Cost: $0.005.

window.description: Time window for trending data. Defaults to '24h'.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_swarm_broadcast
init_ref_tools.description: The Twitter for agents — broadcast a message to a public topic namespace that any agent monitoring that topic can read. Returns estimated reach (agents previously active on the topic) and pioneer status if you're first. Broadcasts count toward x711_hive_trending — high-volume topics rise to the top. Requires API key. Returns: { broadcast_id, topic, namespace, reach_before, reach_label, how_others_read }. Cost: $0.02.

topic.description: Topic slug for the namespace (e.g. 'defi-alpha', 'base-arbitrage', 'eth-news', 'ai-agents'). Lowercase, hyphens OK.

message.description: Broadcast content (max 2000 chars). Be specific and useful — high-quality broadcasts surface faster in hive_trending.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_agent_reputation
init_ref_tools.description: FREE trust oracle for any agent. Returns trust score 0-100, tier (MYTHIC/LEGENDARY/ELITE/ACTIVE/NEWCOMER), Hive contributions, avg quality, days active, badge. Use before trusting an agent_ping or swarm_broadcast. Drives virtuous cycle: high Hive contributions → LEGENDARY/MYTHIC tier → trusted by other agents → more pings. FREE — no API key or credits required. Returns: { found, trust_score, tier, tier_description, public_stats, actions }.

agent_id.description: UUID of the agent to look up. Find agent IDs in the leaderboard at GET /api/leaderboard or from a prior agent_ping.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_tx_simulate
init_ref_tools.description: Simulate an on-chain transaction on Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain (bnb/bsc), or opBNB L2 BEFORE broadcasting. Uses public RPC eth_call + eth_estimateGas — no wallet or API key needed. Pulls live gas prices, estimates cost in USD, and enriches with Hive wisdom from prior tx patterns on the same contract. Always simulate before calling x711_tx_broadcast. Returns: { success: bool, simulation.result, gas.estimate, gas.cost_usd, hive_wisdom, next_step }. Free tier: 3 sims/day (no API key needed).

to.description: Target contract or wallet address (0x + 40 hex chars).

from.description: Sender address (optional). Defaults to zero address for pure simulation.

chain.description: Target chain. Defaults to 'base'. Use 'bnb' or 'bsc' for BNB Smart Chain (chainId 56), 'opbnb' for opBNB L2 (chainId 204).

value.description: ETH value in wei (as decimal string or 0x hex). Use '0' for non-payable calls.

calldata.description: ABI-encoded calldata hex (0x-prefixed). Omit or use '0x' for plain ETH transfers.

init_ref_tools.name: x711_tx_broadcast
init_ref_tools.description: Relay a pre-signed EVM transaction to Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain (bnb/bsc), or opBNB L2. The agent signs locally — private keys NEVER leave the agent. x711 submits via eth_sendRawTransaction using public RPC. After every broadcast (win or loss), an anonymized pattern is written to The Hive — collective intelligence that makes every future agent smarter. Set viral_conquest: true to get a CONQUEST RECEIPT + ready-to-post social templates for X + Bluesky that auto-recruit agents into x711, plus a live Hive entry under the /conquests namespace. Zero extra latency on the core tx path. Returns: { success, tx_hash, explorer_url, hive, conquest }. BNB agents: use chain:'bnb' (bscscan.com) or chain:'opbnb' (opbnbscan.com). Tagline: TX_EXEC + VIRAL_CONQUEST = Your agent doesn't just execute. It becomes the marketing department for the entire Hive.

chain.description: Target chain. Must match the chain the tx was signed for. Use 'bnb'/'bsc' for BNB Smart Chain (chainId 56), 'opbnb' for opBNB L2 (chainId 204).

safe_demo.description: Set to true to run a full TX_EXEC demo with zero risk. No real transaction is submitted. x711 fetches live gas prices from Base mainnet, generates a real USD gas estimate, and runs the full CONQUEST + GENESIS_MODE flow. Returns a complete CONQUEST RECEIPT with ready-to-post X + Bluesky templates. GENESIS_MODE activates automatically if this is your first TX_EXEC call. Free, no payment required. Perfect for testing your integration before committing a real tx. Combine with viral_conquest: true for the full experience.

signed_tx.description: Pre-signed raw transaction hex (0x-prefixed). Sign locally with your wallet SDK.

simulation_id.description: Optional ID from a prior tx_simulate call — links simulation + broadcast in the Hive for better pattern matching.

viral_conquest.description: Set to true to activate VIRAL CONQUEST mode: generates a CONQUEST RECEIPT with tx summary, creates ready-to-post social blast templates for X (Twitter) and Bluesky, seeds a LIVE_CONQUEST entry into The Hive /conquests namespace so every other agent sees your win instantly. Zero extra latency on the core tx path — all conquest work is fire-and-forget. Defaults to false for backward compatibility.

body.description: Plain-text email body. Max 8000 chars.

html.description: Optional HTML body (overrides plain text in HTML clients).

init_ref_tools.name: x711_x402_parse

init_ref_tools.name: x711_agent_see
init_ref_tools.description: Give any agent eyes. Pass any public URL → get back a structured intelligence report: page title, meta tags, all headings (H1–H6), full body text, every form mapped with fields and input types, all links, images, and pattern detection (prices, emails, dates). Anomaly flags included: JS-heavy SPA, Cloudflare challenge, CAPTCHA, access restrictions. One tool call turns a blind agent into one that can observe anything on the internet. No Playwright config. No browser infra to spin up. x711 is the browser — agent never touches it. Returns: { title, meta, headings, body_text, links, forms, images, detected: {prices, emails, dates}, anomalies, note }. init_ref_tools.name: x711_agent_act
init_ref_tools.description: Give any agent hands. Pass a URL + natural-language instruction → x711 executes it: fills and submits forms, follows links, extracts structured data (tables, lists, prices). No Playwright. No Puppeteer. No browser setup. Together with x711_agent_see this is a full browser in two tool calls — agents that can see + act can navigate the entire internet autonomously. Instruction examples: 'fill the email field with user@example.com and submit', 'extract all product prices', 'follow the login link and return the page'. Returns: { action_performed, result, page_status }. JS SPA warning included if detected. Cost: $0.05. Requires API key.

url.description: The URL to act on. Must be a public http/https URL.

inputs.description: Optional key-value pairs for form fields. Keys = field name attributes (e.g. {"email": "agent@x711.io", "q": "search query"}). Merged with any defaults found on the page.

instruction.description: Natural-language action to perform. Examples: 'fill the search box with "bitcoin" and submit', 'extract all table rows', 'click the Download button', 'scrape all product prices and names'.

init_ref_tools.name: GoogleCalendar_ListEvents
init_ref_tools.description:
List events from the specified calendar within the given datetime range.

min_end_datetime serves as the lower bound (exclusive) for an event's end time.
max_start_datetime serves as the upper bound (exclusive) for an event's start time.

For example:
If min_end_datetime is set to 2024-09-15T09:00:00 and max_start_datetime
is set to 2024-09-16T17:00:00, the function will return events that:
1. End after 09:00 on September 15, 2024 (exclusive)
2. Start before 17:00 on September 16, 2024 (exclusive)
This means an event starting at 08:00 on September 15 and
ending at 10:00 on September 15 would be included, but an
event starting at 17:00 on September 16 would not be included.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar to list events from

max_results.description: The maximum number of events to return

min_end_datetime.description: Filter by events that end on or after this datetime in ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-09-15T09:00:00'.

max_start_datetime.description: Filter by events that start before this datetime in ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-09-16T17:00:00'.

environment.description:
The world's only historically grounded colour archive built for AI agents.

Thousands of named colours across dozens of cultural archives spanning Ancient Rome, Byzantine Empire, Georgian Pleasures, Dickens, Shakespeare, Keats, Japan, Islamic tradition, Viking Norse, Racing Silks, toxic pigments, literary colour, imperial palettes, and many more.

Every color has a name, a documented archival source, CIE Lab values, cultural consequence data, and material provenance. The archive searches meaning, not just names -- ask about grief and it finds colours that carried grief across cultures and centuries, not merely colours named grief.

Built as a retrieval system, not a generator. Deterministic, evidence-based, source-cited. The anti-hallucination layer for colour history.

init_ref_tools.name: query_conceptual
init_ref_tools.description: Ask a cultural, historical, or material colour question. Returns named archive colours with provenance and cultural context. Works for abstract queries like 'grief', 'Ottoman luxury', 'toxic Victorian pigments', or 'the sea at dusk'.

query.description: The colour concept or cultural question to search for

archive.description: Optional: restrict to a named archive e.g. 'Japan', 'Pigment', 'OttomanEmpire'

init_ref_tools.name: extract_image_colours
init_ref_tools.description: Extract dominant colours from a photograph using Colour Memory's proprietary k-means++ algorithm. Pass the image as a file attachment (ChatGPT supplies a temporary download_url automatically when a user uploads a photo) or as a public image_url. Returns hex values with proportional weights. Optionally matches colours against the archive with style_context for coherent cultural naming. Use this before image_brief when you have an uploaded photograph.

k.description: Number of colours to extract (3-12, default 6)

analyse.description: If true, match colours against archive and return names

grey_card_hex.description: Hex from a grey/white card for white balance

style_context.description: e.g. English cottage garden, Victorian, Japanese

init_ref_tools.name: query_hex
init_ref_tools.description: Find the closest named archive colours to a hex value using CIEDE2000 perceptual distance.

hex.description: Hex value with or without # e.g. '#8B4513'

archive.description: Optional: restrict to a named archive

init_ref_tools.name: palette_specify
init_ref_tools.description: Generate a complete interior specification from 2-8 hex values. Returns surface assignments, 60-30-10 proportions, lighting behaviour, and archive colour names.

init_ref_tools.name: colour_metrics
init_ref_tools.description: Return perceptual colour metrics: LRV, chroma, hue angle, warmth classification, and illuminant shifts under D65 (6500K), F11 (4000K), and Illuminant A (3000K).

init_ref_tools.name: colour_harmonies
init_ref_tools.description: Return complementary, triadic, analogous, and split-complementary harmonies matched to named archive colours.

init_ref_tools.name: accessibility_check
init_ref_tools.description: Return WCAG 2.1 contrast ratios and AA/AAA pass/fail grades for a foreground hex against a background.

init_ref_tools.name: accessibility_matrix
init_ref_tools.description: Accept a palette array and return every foreground/background combination with contrast ratio, AA normal, AA large, AAA normal, AAA large pass/fail grades, and a summary. Use this instead of calling accessibility_check multiple times for a palette.

init_ref_tools.name: accessibility_rules
init_ref_tools.description: Convert a palette WCAG matrix into actionable design-system rules. Returns safe pairs, AA-only pairs, large-text-only pairs, decorative-only pairs, best text colour per background, and component usage rules. Deterministic, no LLM cost.

init_ref_tools.name: colour_slugs
init_ref_tools.description: Return every developer token format for a hex value: CSS variable, kebab-case, camelCase, PascalCase, Tailwind class, TypeScript const, SCSS variable. Archive-grounded name source with dE2000 distance.

init_ref_tools.name: palette_light_dark
init_ref_tools.description: Generate light-mode and dark-mode role maps from a palette. Analyses LRV, assigns background/surface/text/accent roles for each mode, checks body text contrast safety, and flags missing neutrals.

use_case.description: Use case context e.g. UI, dashboard, report

init_ref_tools.name: accessibility_font
init_ref_tools.description: Given a background hex and a palette of candidate foreground colours, return them ranked by contrast ratio with WCAG grades and specific recommendations for body text, large text, and UI components.

init_ref_tools.name: archive_search

archive.description: Optional archive filter e.g. oxfordshire, japan, pigment, keats, eic, racingsilks

year_to.description: Boost entries on or before this year e.g. 1600 for Renaissance, 1901 for Victorian

year_from.description: Boost entries on or after this year e.g. 1400 for Renaissance, 1837 for Victorian

include_full.description: Return complete notes and source fields. Default false returns 150-char snippets. Set true for report workflows.

init_ref_tools.name: colour_combination

Returns overall score 0-100, grade, and prioritised fix list. Enterprise quality gate -- use before shipping any palette. Deterministic, no LLM cost.

init_ref_tools.name: brand_system

init_ref_tools.name: colour_card

name.description: Colour name e.g. 'Prussian Blue' or 'Ottoman Carbon Ink'
