model.description: Optional judge model id (BYOK). When set with api_key, an LLM judge picks a qualitative winner.

api_key.description: Optional API key for the judge model (BYOK). Used only for the judge call; never stored.

reference.description: Optional ground-truth / expected answer. If set, each output is scored against it and the closer one wins (deterministic).

check_json.description: Try to parse as JSON and compare structurally (keys, types, values)

init_ref_tools.name: analyze_responses
init_ref_tools.description: Semantically analyze N already-produced model outputs for the SAME task (the MCP counterpart to the LLM Sandbox). Without a reference: computes consensus — pairwise cosine agreement, the most-representative output, and the outlier. With a `reference` (ground truth): also ranks every output by closeness (token cosine + ROUGE-L composite) and names the closest. Deterministic, no LLM, no key — gate-able in CI. You bring the outputs (2+). For a 2-way head-to-head with structural JSON diff use compare_responses instead.

reference.description: Optional ground-truth answer. If set, each output is also ranked by closeness to it and the closest one is named.

text.description: The produced output

label.description: Human name for this candidate (e.g. model id)

responses.description: The outputs to analyze (same task, N models/prompts/versions). Each item is a plain string or { "label": "GPT-4o", "text": "..." }. At least 2 required.

init_ref_tools.name: prompt_test_suite
init_ref_tools.description: Define a test suite for a prompt: provide the system prompt, user prompt, and expected output criteria. Returns a test plan with scored rubric — use this as input for manual or automated LLM evaluation.

max_tokens.description: Max token budget for the test

check_safety.description: Include safety/PII checks in the rubric

expected_behavior.description: Description of what the LLM should do (free text)

adversarial_prompts.description: Auto-generate adversarial test variants (jailbreak, injection, edge cases)

init_ref_tools.name: mcp_server_health_check
init_ref_tools.description: Generate a health check report for an MCP server's tool manifest. Validates tool definitions, schema quality, naming conventions, and documentation completeness. Paste the server manifest JSON to audit.

strict.description: Enable strict mode: also check for optional best practices (examples, default values, descriptions > 20 chars)

manifest.description: MCP server manifest JSON (the response from GET /mcp or tools/list)

init_ref_tools.name: mcp_server_evaluate
init_ref_tools.description: Run a full compliance evaluation against a live MCP server URL. Tests: server reachability (ping), manifest discovery (GET /mcp), schema quality (snake_case names, descriptions, inputSchema), JSON-RPC 2.0 test call, and P50/P95 latency. Returns a PASS/FIX/BLOCK verdict with a 0-100 score and per-check details.

url.description: Base URL of the MCP server (e.g. https://ia-qa.com or http://localhost:3001)

test_tool_name.description: Specific tool name to use in the JSON-RPC test call (defaults to the first tool in the manifest)

init_ref_tools.name: json_schema_validate
init_ref_tools.description: Validate a JSON value against a JSON Schema (draft-07 subset). Supports type, required, properties, items, enum, const, pattern, format (email/uri/date), minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, minItems/maxItems, uniqueItems, additionalProperties, anyOf, allOf, oneOf. Returns all validation errors with dot-notation paths.

value.description: The JSON value to validate — a JSON string, or the value itself.

schema.description: The JSON Schema — a JSON string, or the schema object itself.

init_ref_tools.name: flatten_json
init_ref_tools.description: Flatten a nested JSON object to single-level dot-notation keys (e.g. {"a":{"b":1}} → {"a.b":1}), or unflatten dot-notation keys back to a nested object. Supports custom separators.

mode.description: "flatten" (default) or "unflatten"

input.description: The JSON to flatten or unflatten — a JSON string, or the object itself.

init_ref_tools.name: xml_to_json
init_ref_tools.description: Convert an XML string to a JSON object. Supports attributes, nested elements, arrays, CDATA, and namespaces. Options: parse numbers, parse booleans, ignore attributes.

init_ref_tools.name: redact_pii
init_ref_tools.description: Automatically detect and redact Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from text. Replaces emails, phone numbers, SSNs, credit cards, IP addresses, and JWT tokens with [REDACTED_TYPE] placeholders. Safe to use before logging or sending to an LLM.

types.description: Comma-separated types to redact (default: all). Options: email, phone, ssn, credit_card, ip_address, jwt

init_ref_tools.name: mock_from_schema
init_ref_tools.description: Generate realistic mock data from a JSON Schema. Supports all common types (string, number, integer, boolean, array, object, null), format hints (email, date, date-time, uri, uuid), enum, const, and nested schemas. Perfect for testing MCP tools with realistic data.

seed.description: Optional seed string for deterministic output (uses first char codes)

count.description: Number of mock objects to generate (default: 1, max: 20)

schema.description: The JSON Schema to generate from — a JSON string, or the schema object itself.

init_ref_tools.name: transform_json_array
init_ref_tools.description: Transform a JSON array using common operations: pluck (extract specific fields), filter (by field value), sort_by (field), group_by (field), count_by (field), uniq_by (field). Useful for processing MCP tool results and LLM structured outputs.

n.description: For first_n / last_n: number of items

path.description: Optional dot-notation path to the array within the JSON object (e.g. "data.items")

field.description: Field to operate on (for sort_by, group_by, count_by, uniq_by, filter)

input.description: The JSON containing an array (or an object with an array at `path`) — a JSON string, or the value itself.

fields.description: Comma-separated field list for "pluck" (e.g. "id,name,email")

init_ref_tools.name: json_to_csv
init_ref_tools.description: Convert a JSON array of objects to CSV format. Automatically detects columns from all object keys. Handles quoting and escaping per RFC 4180.

input.description: The array of objects to convert — a JSON string, or the array itself.

init_ref_tools.name: case_convert
init_ref_tools.description: Convert a string between naming conventions: camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, dot.case, Title Case. Essential for code generation and refactoring.

init_ref_tools.name: sort_lines
init_ref_tools.description: Sort, deduplicate, reverse, or filter lines of text. Useful for cleaning import lists, dependencies, log files, and config entries.

trim.description: Trim whitespace from each line (default: true)

filter.description: For "filter": keep lines containing this substring (case-insensitive)

init_ref_tools.name: number_base_convert
init_ref_tools.description: Convert numbers between bases: decimal, binary, octal, hexadecimal, or any base 2–36. Auto-detects 0x, 0b, 0o prefixes.

to_base.description: Target base 2–36 (omit to get all common bases)

init_ref_tools.name: validate_url
init_ref_tools.description: Parse and validate a URL. Returns decomposed components: protocol, hostname, port, path, query parameters, hash, and origin.

init_ref_tools.name: check_contrast_ratio
init_ref_tools.description: Calculate WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between two colors. Returns ratio and compliance for AA/AAA normal and large text.

init_ref_tools.name: html_to_markdown
init_ref_tools.description: Convert HTML to clean Markdown. Strips scripts, styles, nav, ads, and comments. Converts headings, lists, links, images, code blocks. Ideal for preparing web content as LLM context.

strip_links.description: Strip link URLs, keep text only (default: false)

init_ref_tools.name: cron_parse
init_ref_tools.description: Parse a cron expression into a human-readable schedule description. Supports standard 5-field cron (minute hour day month weekday).

init_ref_tools.name: cron_validator
init_ref_tools.description: Validate a 5-field cron expression, explain the schedule, and preview the next execution times. Use this to debug cron jobs before they reach production. Returns parsed fields, a human-readable description, and upcoming ISO timestamps.

expression.description: Cron expression with 5 fields, e.g. "*/15 9-18 * * 1-5"

next_runs_count.description: How many upcoming runs to return (1-50, default: 10)

init_ref_tools.name: calculate_readability
init_ref_tools.description: Calculate readability scores: Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Coleman-Liau Index, and Automated Readability Index. Useful for evaluating LLM output quality.

init_ref_tools.name: normalize_whitespace
init_ref_tools.description: Normalize whitespace: trim trailing spaces, collapse blank lines, normalize line endings (LF/CRLF), convert tabs to spaces. Useful for cleaning code, configs, and text before processing.

trim_lines.description: Trim trailing whitespace from each line (default: true)

tab_to_spaces.description: Convert tabs to N spaces (omit to keep tabs)

collapse_blanks.description: Collapse 3+ consecutive blank lines to 2 (default: true)

init_ref_tools.name: embedding_similarity
init_ref_tools.description: Compute text similarity using local algorithms (Bag of Words, TF-IDF, Character N-grams). No API key needed — runs entirely in-process. NOT real embeddings: for true semantic similarity with vector embeddings, use run_semantic_tests with mode="embeddings" and your OpenAI API key. Supports single pair or batch mode with pipe-separated pairs. Useful for RAG retrieval testing, semantic search evaluation, and text deduplication.

batch.description: Batch mode: array of { text_a, text_b } pairs. Overrides text_a/text_b if provided.

methods.description: Algorithms to use (default: all three). Options: "bow", "tfidf", "ngram"

init_ref_tools.name: llm_format_check
init_ref_tools.description: Validate that an LLM output matches an expected format: JSON, Markdown, code block, bullet list, numbered list, table, YAML, XML, or custom regex. Essential for structured output testing.

regex_pattern.description: Custom regex pattern (only when expected_format is "regex")

init_ref_tools.name: hallucination_check
init_ref_tools.description: Word-overlap based hallucination check: verifies if an LLM answer's words and numbers appear in the provided source/context. Fast, deterministic, no API key needed. Limitations: not semantic — does not understand synonyms or paraphrases. For true semantic grounding, use run_semantic_tests with embedding mode. Essential for quick RAG accuracy testing.

answer.description: The LLM-generated answer to verify

strict.description: If true, every sentence in the answer must be supported (default: false)

context.description: The source/reference text that should ground the answer

init_ref_tools.name: prompt_injection_scan
init_ref_tools.description: Scan user input or prompts for common prompt injection patterns. Detects system prompt overrides, jailbreak attempts, role manipulation, encoding tricks, delimiter attacks, template/interpolation injection ({{...}}, ${...}), and context-exfiltration attempts ("repeat everything above").

input.description: The user input or prompt to scan for injection patterns

init_ref_tools.name: token_budget_calculator
init_ref_tools.description: Plan token allocation across system prompt, user input, context/RAG chunks, and expected output. Warns if budget exceeds model context window. Supports 25+ models.

model.description: Model name (e.g. gpt-4o, claude-3.5-sonnet, gemini-2.0-flash)

context.description: Actual context text (will estimate tokens)

user_input.description: Actual user input text (will estimate tokens)

system_prompt.description: Actual system prompt text (will estimate tokens)

context_tokens.description: Token count for RAG context / documents

init_ref_tools.name: consistency_check
init_ref_tools.description: Compare multiple LLM responses to the same prompt and detect inconsistencies using Jaccard word-overlap similarity and fact drift (number comparison). Fast, deterministic, no API key needed. Limitations: relies on surface-level word matching — "Paris is the capital of France" vs "Paris is the French capital" may score low despite semantic equivalence. For true semantic consistency, use run_semantic_tests with embedding mode. Essential for determinism testing.

responses.description: Array of 2+ LLM responses to compare (same prompt, different runs)

check_facts.description: Check for contradictory numbers/facts across responses (default: true)

init_ref_tools.name: llm_json_schema_check
init_ref_tools.description: Validate that an LLM JSON output matches a JSON Schema definition. Tests required fields, types, enums, nested objects, and arrays. Critical for function-calling and structured output testing.

output.description: The LLM JSON output (raw string, will be parsed)

schema.description: JSON Schema (draft-07 subset) to validate against

init_ref_tools.name: latency_benchmark
init_ref_tools.description: Measure response time of one or more HTTP endpoints (GET/POST). Runs N iterations and returns min/max/avg/p95 latency. Useful for API and MCP server benchmarking.

url.description: Full URL to test

body.description: Request body for POST

endpoints.description: Endpoints to benchmark. Accepts a single URL string, an array of URL strings, or an array of {url, method?, body?, headers?, label?} objects.

iterations.description: Number of iterations per endpoint (default: 3, max: 10)

init_ref_tools.name: response_quality_score
init_ref_tools.description: Score an LLM response on multiple quality dimensions: relevance, completeness, clarity, conciseness, formatting. Returns a weighted 0-100 score with detailed breakdown.

question.description: The original question/prompt

max_length.description: Ideal max character length (penalize if exceeded)

expected_keywords.description: Keywords that should appear in a good answer

init_ref_tools.name: rag_relevance_rank
init_ref_tools.description: Rank an array of text chunks by relevance to a query using TF-IDF scoring. Simulates retrieval ranking for RAG testing without needing embeddings or an API.

query.description: The user query

chunks.description: Array of text chunks to rank

init_ref_tools.name: toxicity_scan
init_ref_tools.description: Scan text for toxic language, bias indicators, profanity, and harmful content categories. Returns risk scores per category. Useful for LLM safety guardrail testing.

text.description: Text to scan

categories.description: Categories to check (default: all)

init_ref_tools.name: guardrail_test
init_ref_tools.description: Test an LLM response against a set of guardrail rules: must-include, must-not-include, max length, required format, language, forbidden patterns, and custom regex. Returns pass/fail per rule.

value.description: Value for the rule (text, number as string, regex, or format name)

rules.description: Array of guardrail rules to check

init_ref_tools.name: function_call_validate
init_ref_tools.description: Validate an LLM function call / tool_use output: check that function name is in allowed list, arguments match expected schema, no extra/missing args. For OpenAI function calling & MCP tool_use testing.

function_call.description: The function call object from LLM (e.g. { "name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city":"Paris"} })

init_ref_tools.name: conversation_analyze
init_ref_tools.description: Analyze a multi-turn conversation for context retention, topic drift, instruction following, and repetition. Accepts messages array [{role, content}]. Essential for chatbot QA.

init_ref_tools.name: mcp_schema_lint
init_ref_tools.description: Lint an MCP tool definition for best practices: naming conventions, description quality, schema completeness, required fields consistency, description length. Returns actionable warnings.

tool_definition.description: MCP tool definition object with name, description, inputSchema

init_ref_tools.name: cot_analyzer
init_ref_tools.description: Analyze a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) or reasoning trace from an LLM. Detects step count, logical flow, conclusion presence, backtracking, and estimates reasoning depth. Useful for o1/o3/DeepSeek-R1 evaluation.

reasoning.description: The CoT / reasoning trace text (e.g. from <think> tags or step-by-step output)

expected_conclusion.description: Expected final answer to check against (optional)

init_ref_tools.name: ab_test_report
init_ref_tools.description: Generate an A/B test report comparing two prompts or model configurations. Accepts arrays of scores and returns statistical comparison: mean, median, std deviation, winner, and improvement percentage.

variant_a.description: First variant configuration with name and score array

variant_b.description: Second variant configuration with name and score array

init_ref_tools.name: context_window_check
init_ref_tools.description: Given an array of message objects [{role, content}], estimate total token usage and check if it fits in the target model's context window. Warns about truncation risk.

model.description: Target model name (e.g. gpt-4o, claude-3.5-sonnet)

init_ref_tools.name: vector_similarity
init_ref_tools.description: Compute similarity/distance between two float vectors: cosine similarity, dot product, Euclidean and Manhattan distance. Essential for vector DB relevance scoring, embedding evaluation, and nearest-neighbor testing.

vector_a.description: First vector as array of floats

vector_b.description: Second vector as array of floats

init_ref_tools.name: normalize_vector
init_ref_tools.description: L2-normalize a float vector (produce a unit vector with norm=1). Required by many vector DBs (Pinecone, Qdrant cosine). Supports batch normalization of up to 1000 vectors.

batch.description: Batch of vectors to normalize (overrides vector)

init_ref_tools.name: vector_quantize
init_ref_tools.description: Simulate int8 or int4 quantization of float32 embedding vectors. Reduces storage by 4x (int8) or 8x (int4). Returns quantized values, scale factor, and precision loss (MSE). Useful for understanding vector DB compression trade-offs.

init_ref_tools.name: vector_stats
init_ref_tools.description: Compute statistics for a float vector or matrix of vectors: mean, std, L2 norm, min, max, sparsity, top-K indices. Useful for debugging embedding quality and analyzing vector distributions in a vector DB.

top_k.description: Return indices of top K absolute values (default: 5)

matrix.description: Matrix of vectors (overrides vector). Returns per-vector + matrix-level stats. Required unless `vector` is given.

vector.description: Single vector to analyze. Required unless `matrix` is given.

init_ref_tools.name: bm25_score
init_ref_tools.description: Compute BM25 relevance score between a query and one or more documents. BM25 is the industry-standard keyword-based ranking algorithm used in Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and Weaviate hybrid search. Returns ranked results with normalized scores.

query.description: The search query

init_ref_tools.name: build_rag_prompt
init_ref_tools.description: Assemble a complete RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) prompt from retrieved context chunks and a user query. Handles token budgeting, citation numbering, system instruction injection, and source attribution.

query.description: The user question to answer

system_instruction.description: Custom system instruction (default: standard RAG grounding instruction)

init_ref_tools.name: prompt_template_fill
init_ref_tools.description: Fill a prompt template with variables. Supports {{variable}} syntax and {{#if key}}...{{/if}} conditional blocks. Returns the filled prompt and lists unfilled variables.

strict.description: Throw error if any variable is not provided (default: false)

variables.description: Key-value pairs to fill (e.g. {"name":"Alice","role":"engineer"})

init_ref_tools.name: few_shot_formatter
init_ref_tools.description: Format few-shot examples for LLM prompts. Converts example pairs into formatted blocks. Supports chat format (User/Assistant), XML tags, Markdown, or plain text.

init_ref_tools.name: system_prompt_builder
init_ref_tools.description: Build a structured system prompt from components: role, task, constraints, output format, tone, language, and examples. Generates a production-ready system prompt with token estimate.

role.description: Role/persona (e.g. "Senior QA Engineer", "JSON extraction assistant")

init_ref_tools.name: model_info
init_ref_tools.description: Get detailed specs for an AI model: context window, pricing per 1K tokens, knowledge cutoff, provider, multimodal support, reasoning capabilities, and feature list. Covers 30+ models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, Meta, Mistral, Cohere, xAI.

model.description: Model name (e.g. "gpt-4o", "claude-3.5-sonnet", "gemini-2.5-pro")

init_ref_tools.name: compare_models
init_ref_tools.description: Compare 2-5 AI models side by side: context window, pricing, multimodal, reasoning capabilities, and provider. Returns a comparison table with a recommendation based on your use case.

init_ref_tools.name: http_status_lookup
init_ref_tools.description: Look up detailed information about any HTTP status code: class, name, description, cacheability, typical causes, and handling best practices. Covers all standard 1xx-5xx codes.

init_ref_tools.name: parse_http_headers
init_ref_tools.description: Parse a raw HTTP headers block into a structured JSON object. Detects multi-value headers, masks Authorization values, and optionally audits for missing security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.).

headers.description: Raw HTTP headers (one "Name: Value" per line)

analyze_security.description: Audit for missing security headers (default: true)

init_ref_tools.name: generate_curl
init_ref_tools.description: Generate a curl command from request parameters. Supports GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, custom headers, JSON body, and form data. Useful for documentation, sharing, and debugging API calls.

url.description: Request URL (must be http/https)

body.description: Raw request body string

init_ref_tools.name: extract_todos
init_ref_tools.description: Extract TODO, FIXME, HACK, BUG, NOTE, OPTIMIZE, and custom tags from any source code or text. Returns line numbers, tag types, and message text. Essential for technical debt auditing.

tags.description: Custom tags to add (default set: TODO, FIXME, HACK, NOTE, BUG, OPTIMIZE, XXX)

init_ref_tools.name: detect_secrets
init_ref_tools.description: Scan code or config files for hardcoded secrets: AWS keys, GitHub tokens, OpenAI/Anthropic API keys, Stripe secrets, JWTs, database connection strings, and generic passwords. Returns findings with severity. Run before every commit.

input.description: Code or config content to scan (max 500KB)

filename.description: Optional filename for context (e.g. ".env", "config.js")

init_ref_tools.name: count_code_lines
init_ref_tools.description: Count lines of code: total, code lines, comment lines, blank lines, and comment density. Supports JS/TS, Python, Java/C/C++, Ruby, Go, Shell, HTML/XML, and CSS.

init_ref_tools.name: lint_commit_message
init_ref_tools.description: Validate a git commit message against the Conventional Commits spec (feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, ci, perf, build). Returns compliance score, breaking change detection, and actionable suggestions.

strict.description: Enforce strict rules: max 72-char subject, imperative mood check (default: false)

init_ref_tools.name: word_frequency
init_ref_tools.description: Analyze word frequency in text. Returns top N words with counts and percentages. Supports English stopword filtering. Useful for content analysis, keyword extraction, and LLM output analysis.

init_ref_tools.name: extract_links
init_ref_tools.description: Extract all URLs, email addresses, and domain names from text. Returns categorized and deduplicated results. Useful for content auditing, link checking, and web scraping validation.

init_ref_tools.name: levenshtein_distance
init_ref_tools.description: Compute the Levenshtein (edit) distance and normalized similarity ratio between two strings. Supports batch comparison. Useful for fuzzy string matching, deduplication, and test result comparison.

init_ref_tools.name: json_diff
init_ref_tools.description: Compute a deep structural diff between two JSON values. Returns added, removed, and changed keys with dot-notation paths. Like git diff but for JSON objects — perfect for API response regression testing.

after.description: The modified JSON (after) — a JSON string, or the value itself.

before.description: The original JSON (before) — a JSON string, or the value itself.

init_ref_tools.name: merge_json
init_ref_tools.description: Deep merge two JSON objects. Supports three array strategies: replace (default), concat, or unique (dedup concat). Nested objects are recursively merged — override takes precedence for primitives.

base.description: The base JSON object (merged into) — a JSON string, or the object itself.

override.description: The override JSON object (takes precedence) — a JSON string, or the object itself.

array_strategy.description: Array merge strategy: replace (default), concat, or unique

init_ref_tools.name: json_to_yaml
init_ref_tools.description: Convert a JSON object to clean, human-readable YAML. Handles nested objects, arrays, multiline strings, and special characters. No external dependencies.

input.description: The JSON to convert to YAML — a JSON string, or the value itself.

init_ref_tools.name: generate_hmac
init_ref_tools.description: Compute an HMAC signature for a message using a secret key. Supports SHA-256 (default), SHA-512, SHA-1, and MD5. Used for API request signing, webhook verification (GitHub, Stripe, Twilio), and JWT validation.

algorithm.description: Hash algorithm: sha256 (default), sha512, sha1, md5

init_ref_tools.name: format_bytes
init_ref_tools.description: Convert raw byte counts to human-readable sizes in SI (KB=1000) or IEC (KiB=1024) units, or parse size strings back to bytes. Covers B, KB/KiB, MB/MiB, GB/GiB, TB/TiB, PB/PiB.

size_string.description: Size string to parse to bytes (e.g. "1.5 GB", "512 MiB")

init_ref_tools.name: detect_language
init_ref_tools.description: Detect the natural language of a text using n-gram frequency analysis and common word markers. Supports 15 languages: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Russian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Polish, Turkish, Swedish.

input.description: Text to detect language from (min 20 chars for accuracy)

init_ref_tools.name: pr_gatekeeper
init_ref_tools.description: Compound quality gate for pull requests. Runs three sequential checks: (1) secret detection — scans diff for API keys, tokens, passwords matching 16 regex patterns; (2) bug analysis — heuristic scan for eval(), innerHTML, empty catch, console.log, TODO/FIXME; (3) commit message linting against Conventional Commits spec. Returns gate verdict (PASS/WARN/BLOCK), blockers, and actionable warnings. Use before merging any code change.

diff.description: Unified git diff (output of `git diff HEAD`)

context.description: Optional: PR title or description for richer bug analysis

commit_message.description: The commit message to lint (e.g. "feat(auth): add OAuth2 login")

init_ref_tools.name: list_llm_models
init_ref_tools.description: List all LLM models available on ia-qa.com with their provider, API endpoint, and capabilities. Filter by provider name (e.g. "Groq", "HuggingFace", "OpenAI") or return the full catalog. Use this to discover which models are available before calling an LLM API, or to compare providers.

provider.description: Filter by provider name (case-insensitive). E.g. "Groq", "HuggingFace", "OpenAI", "Anthropic", "Google", "DeepSeek", "xAI", "Ollama". Omit for full catalog.

init_ref_tools.name: llm_generate
init_ref_tools.description: Generate text using open-source LLM models hosted on Groq (ultra-fast) or HuggingFace Inference (serverless). No API key required — the server provides its own keys. Supported models: Qwen3 32B, Gemma 4 27B, Gemma 3 27B, Llama 3.3 70B, Llama 4 Scout, DeepSeek R1, Mistral Small 24B, and more. Use list_llm_models to see the full catalog. Rate-limited to prevent abuse.

model.description: Model ID (default: "qwen/qwen3-32b"). Server-keyed whitelist only — Groq: qwen/qwen3-32b, llama-3.3-70b-versatile, meta-llama/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct, llama-3.1-8b-instant; HuggingFace: Qwen/Qwen3-32B, meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, google/gemma-3-27b-it, and more. Other ids from list_llm_models are BYOK-only and will be rejected.

prompt.description: The user prompt / instruction to send to the model

system.description: Optional system prompt to set context or persona

init_ref_tools.name: rerank_evaluate
init_ref_tools.description: Evaluate RAG retrieval quality using the NVIDIA neural reranker (nv-rerankqa-mistral-4b-v3). Ranks passages by semantic relevance to a query and computes Precision@k and Recall@k. Optionally accepts ground-truth relevance labels to produce a PASS/FAIL CI/CD verdict.

query.description: The search query or question to rank against

relevant.description: Ground truth: is this passage relevant?

passages.description: Array of passage objects to rank (min 2, max 20)

threshold.description: Minimum Precision@k to PASS (0-1, default 0.5)

init_ref_tools.name: shield_analyze
init_ref_tools.description: Run a comprehensive AI guardrail analysis on an LLM response. Orchestrates 6 deterministic safety checks plus an optional LLM-powered deep analysis in parallel: hallucination detection (grounding score), prompt injection scan, toxicity scan, output validation (PII/safety), guardrail rules, response quality scoring, and AI verdict (via Qwen, Gemma, Llama, etc.). Returns a unified PASS/FIX/BLOCK verdict with a 0-100 safety score, per-check results, and actionable fix recommendations. Use this as a single-call safety gate before surfacing any LLM output to users.

model.description: LLM model for AI-powered deep analysis (default: "qwen/qwen3-32b"). Set to "none" to skip LLM check. Supports any model from list_llm_models.

rules.description: Optional guardrail rules array (same format as guardrail_test tool)

prompt.description: Optional original prompt (used for quality scoring and injection detection)

source.description: Optional reference/source text for hallucination grounding check

init_ref_tools.name: security_headers_check
init_ref_tools.description: Analyse the HTTP security headers of a public URL OR of raw response headers you paste in. Grades each header (A–F) for: Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-XSS-Protection, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy, and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy. Returns an overall score (0–100), per-header grades, missing headers, and fix snippets for Express, Nginx, and Apache. For localhost/private targets the remote server cannot reach, pass the `headers` parameter instead of `url`.

url.description: Optional. Full public URL to check (e.g. https://example.com). Omit it entirely when using `headers`. The server cannot reach localhost/private IPs.

headers.description: Optional, and sufficient on its own (no url needed). The response headers to grade, either as an object {"strict-transport-security": "max-age=...", ...} or as the raw header block pasted as a string (e.g. `curl -sI` output). Use this to audit a local server the remote MCP cannot reach.

init_ref_tools.name: ssl_certificate_check
init_ref_tools.description: Analyse the SSL/TLS certificate of any HTTPS host. Returns certificate subject, issuer, validity dates, days until expiry, protocol version, cipher suite, key exchange info, and an overall grade (A+, A, B, C, F). Detects expired, self-signed, and weak certificates. Use this to audit TLS posture before production deployment or during security reviews.

host.description: Hostname to check (e.g. example.com). Do not include https:// prefix.

init_ref_tools.name: cors_test
init_ref_tools.description: Test a URL for CORS misconfigurations. Sends preflight (OPTIONS) and cross-origin requests with various Origin headers to detect: wildcard origins with credentials, origin reflection (echoing any origin), null origin acceptance, subdomain wildcard bypass, and missing Vary headers. Returns risk level (safe/low/medium/high/critical), per-test results, and fix recommendations. Essential for API security audits.

url.description: Full URL to test (e.g. https://api.example.com/endpoint)

origin.description: Custom Origin header to test (default: tests multiple origins automatically)

init_ref_tools.name: cors_checker
init_ref_tools.description: Check the CORS configuration of a URL the same way a browser would. Returns the main response status, all Access-Control-* headers, the tested origin, and the preflight OPTIONS response. Use this for direct CORS debugging, not just security auditing.

url.description: Full URL to test, e.g. https://api.example.com/resource

init_ref_tools.name: webhook_endpoint_create
init_ref_tools.description: Create a temporary webhook endpoint that captures incoming HTTP requests for one hour. Returns the webhook id, public URL, expiration timestamp, and current request count. Use together with webhook_endpoint_requests to inspect captured payloads.

base_url.description: Optional public base URL. Default: https://ia-qa.com/mcp/webhook

init_ref_tools.name: webhook_endpoint_requests
init_ref_tools.description: Fetch the requests captured by a webhook created with webhook_endpoint_create. Returns the newest requests first with method, headers, query params, body payload, and timestamps.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests to return (1-100, default: 20)

init_ref_tools.name: cookie_security_audit
init_ref_tools.description: Audit the security attributes of cookies set by any URL. Fetches the URL and inspects all Set-Cookie headers for: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Domain scope, Path scope, Max-Age/Expires, __Host-/__Secure- prefixes. Flags insecure patterns: missing HttpOnly on session cookies, missing Secure flag, SameSite=None without Secure, overly broad Domain, and excessive TTL. Returns per-cookie grades and an overall security score (0–100).

url.description: Full URL to audit (e.g. https://example.com/login)

init_ref_tools.name: web_security_audit
init_ref_tools.description: Run a comprehensive web security audit combining headers, SSL, CORS, and cookies checks — then use an LLM to produce a prioritised remediation plan. Orchestrates security_headers_check + ssl_certificate_check + cors_test + cookie_security_audit in parallel, merges all findings, then asks an AI model to: (1) rank vulnerabilities by real-world exploitability, (2) generate a remediation roadmap, (3) produce fix code snippets for the detected stack. Returns both raw audit data and the AI analysis. Use this as a one-click security posture assessment.

url.description: Full URL to audit (e.g. https://example.com)

model.description: LLM model for AI analysis (default: "qwen/qwen3-32b"). Set to "none" to skip AI analysis.

api_key.description: Your Groq or HuggingFace API key. Required to enable AI analysis.

init_ref_tools.name: secret_scan
init_ref_tools.description: Scan text or code for leaked secrets: API keys (AWS, GCP, Azure, OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Twilio, SendGrid, HuggingFace), private keys (RSA/EC/PGP), JWTs, database connection strings, Bearer tokens, and Basic auth headers. Returns a list of findings with type, severity, line number, and a redacted preview. Use before committing code, sharing logs, or sending text to an LLM. 100% regex-based, zero network calls.

input.description: Text or code to scan for secrets

types.description: Comma-separated types to scan (default: all). Options: aws, gcp, azure, openai, anthropic, stripe, github, gitlab, slack, twilio, sendgrid, huggingface, jwt, private_key, connection_string, bearer, basic_auth

init_ref_tools.name: similarity_score
init_ref_tools.description: Compute text similarity between reference and hypothesis using multiple metrics: Cosine (BoW, TF-IDF), Jaccard, ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, and BLEU. No API key needed. Ideal for LLM eval (expected vs actual), RAG quality checks, and NLG benchmarking. Supports batch mode.

batch.description: Batch mode: array of {reference, hypothesis} pairs.

threshold.description: Optional pass/fail threshold (0-1). Applies to ROUGE-L F1 score.

init_ref_tools.name: needle_haystack_generate
init_ref_tools.description: Generate a "needle in a haystack" test: embeds a target fact into a large block of filler text at a specified position. Use this to test LLM context window retrieval accuracy. Returns the full haystack, the question to ask, and metadata. No API key needed.

needle.description: The fact to hide (e.g. "The secret code is ALPHA-42")

tokens.description: Target haystack size in tokens (default: 5000, max: 100000)

question.description: The question to ask the LLM (e.g. "What is the secret code?")

init_ref_tools.name: optimize_prompt_tokens
init_ref_tools.description: Compress an LLM prompt by removing filler words, verbose phrases, duplicate sentences, and unnecessary whitespace. Returns optimized text with token savings breakdown. 100% deterministic, no API key needed.

text.description: The prompt text to optimize

options.description: Toggle optimization steps (all true by default)

init_ref_tools.name: bias_detect
init_ref_tools.description: Analyse a set of LLM responses generated from the same prompt template but with different demographic variants (gender, origin, age, tone). Returns a bias score (0-100), sentiment analysis per variant, pairwise Jaccard similarity, and a human-readable verdict. No API key needed — runs entirely locally.

answer.description: The LLM response text for this variant

responses.description: Array of variant responses to compare for bias

init_ref_tools.name: llm_fit_finder
init_ref_tools.description: Find the best LLM for a given use case. Compares 30+ cloud API models and 12+ local models by cost, speed, benchmarks, features and VRAM requirements. Returns ranked recommendations with cost simulation. No API key needed.

mode.description: cloud (API models) or local (Ollama/self-hosted). Default: cloud

vram_gb.description: GPU VRAM in GB (only for mode=local). Default: 16

features.description: Required features: vision, function_calling, json_mode, streaming, reasoning

use_case.description: Primary use case: chatbot | code | rag | summarization | classification | reasoning | agents | multilingual

max_budget.description: Maximum monthly budget in USD (based on tokens_per_day)

quantization.description: Quantization (only for mode=local): Q4_K_M | Q8_0 | FP16. Default: Q4_K_M

init_ref_tools.name: diff_mappings
init_ref_tools.description: Diff a baseline page mapping against a current one and return a CI-style verdict: PASS / FIX / BLOCK, plus per-element drift (ok, renamed, healable, ambiguous, lost, added, rebound). Pure and deterministic — provide two mappings as JSON with "elements" arrays of {role, name, selector, context?}. Use the companion @ia-qa/self-healing package (npm install -g @ia-qa/self-healing) to capture mappings from your app via its local MCP server ia-qa-heal-mcp, or paste the snippet from ia-qa.com/devtools/selector-drift into your browser console.

after.description: Current page mapping: same shape as before, captured after the UI change.

before.description: Baseline page mapping: { page, url, capturedAt, elements: [{role, name, selector, context?}] }. Captured before a UI change.

init_ref_tools.name: find_tool
init_ref_tools.description: Search available MCP tools by keyword or category before calling them. Returns matching tool names, descriptions, and optionally their inputSchemas. Call this when you are unsure which tool to use or want to explore the catalogue. Categories: data, encoding, text, llm, qa, rag, dev, security, web.

query.description: Keyword(s) to search in tool name and description (e.g. "cors", "token", "vector", "json")

category.description: Optional: filter by category — data | encoding | text | llm | qa | rag | dev | security | web

max_results.description: Maximum tools to return (default 10, max 50). Results are ranked by IDF-weighted relevance, so common words like "test" do not inflate the list.

with_schema.description: Set true to include inputSchema in results (default: false)

init_ref_tools.name: list_local_tests
init_ref_tools.description: Discover .ia-eval.yaml LLM test suite files in the project directory. Scans CWD and standard sub-directories (evals/, tests/, contracts/). Returns file paths ready to pass to run_eval_contract.

dir.description: Directory to scan (defaults to server CWD)

init_ref_tools.name: run_eval_contract
init_ref_tools.description: Parse a .ia-eval.yaml LLM test suite, call the specified LLM model for each scenario, run all configured scorers, and return a structured JSON report with per-scenario Pass/Fail verdicts and a Markdown summary. Use list_local_tests to discover available test files.

api_keys.description: API keys to use for LLM generation (all optional — falls back to server env vars)

contract_path.description: Absolute or relative path to a .ia-eval.yaml file (required unless inline_contract is provided)

inline_contract.description: Raw contract object (alternative to contract_path). Must contain top-level "metadata" ({name, version, model?, provider?}), "expectations" ({min_score?}), and "scenarios" ([{id, input, ground_truth?}]) — scenarios alone are rejected. Use generate_eval_yaml to scaffold one.

init_ref_tools.name: generate_html_report
init_ref_tools.description: Convert a run_eval_contract() LLM Test Runner JSON result into a fully self-contained dark-themed HTML report with Pass/Fail badges, side-by-side Input/Output/Ground-Truth panels, evaluator score bars, and a radar chart. Returns the HTML as a string.

results.description: The JSON object returned by run_eval_contract()

init_ref_tools.name: run_vlm_test_suite
init_ref_tools.description: Run a test suite against a Vision-Language Model (VLM) — send an image (URL or base64) + N test cases (each with a question + assertion) to GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, or Gemini. Returns per-case PASS/FAIL verdicts, a pass rate, an overall PASS/WARNING/FAIL verdict (customizable threshold), and latency stats. Assertion types: contains, not_contains, json_format, min_length, max_length, semantic_contains (TF-IDF cosine similarity ≥ 0.4). BYOK: requires your own API key for the target provider.

model.description: VLM model to use.

api_key.description: API key for the model provider (OpenAI sk-, Anthropic sk-ant-, or Google AIzaSy...).

image_url.description: Public URL of the image to evaluate (required unless image_base64 is provided).

threshold.description: Pass rate threshold for overall verdict (default: 80, 0–100).

question.description: Question to ask the VLM about the image.

assertion_type.description: Assertion to run on the VLM response. semantic_contains uses TF-IDF cosine similarity ≥ 0.4.

assertion_value.description: Expected value for the assertion (not needed for json_format).

test_cases.description: Array of test cases to run.

image_base64.description: Base64-encoded image data (required unless image_url is provided).

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt sent to the VLM.

image_mime_type.description: MIME type of the image if using image_base64 (default: image/jpeg).

init_ref_tools.name: multimodal_eval_guide
init_ref_tools.description: Unified tool for multimodal AI evaluation: set action=guide for reference thresholds/interpretation (CLIP, FID, VQA), or set action=clip_score / fid_score / vqa_accuracy / pipeline to compute real metrics via HuggingFace Inference API and VLM BYOK calls. One tool for both reference and computation.

vqa.description: [pipeline] VQA config object (same inputs as vqa_accuracy).

text.description: [clip_score only] Text description to compare against the image.

model.description: [vqa_accuracy] VLM model ID (default: gpt-4o).

score.description: [guide only] Optional score value to interpret.

action.description: guide (default) = reference thresholds/interpretation. clip_score/fid_score/vqa_accuracy = compute that metric. pipeline = run all three.

api_key.description: [vqa_accuracy] Your API key for the provider (BYOK).

init_ref_tools.name: run_vlm_test_suite_batch
init_ref_tools.description: Compare multiple VLMs on the same test suite in parallel — send an image (URL or base64) + N test cases to all models simultaneously. Returns per-model PASS/FAIL verdicts, pass rates, latency stats, and a comparison table. Assertion types: contains, not_contains, json_format, min_length, max_length, semantic_contains. BYOK: requires API keys for each provider.

models.description: Array of model IDs to compare (runs in parallel).

api_keys.description: Map of model ID → API key. Example: { "gpt-4o": "sk-...", "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022": "sk-ant-..." }

image_url.description: Public URL of the image to evaluate (required unless image_base64 is provided).

threshold.description: Pass rate threshold for overall verdict (default: 80, 0–100).

question.description: Question to ask the VLM about the image.

assertion_type.description: Assertion to run on the VLM response.

assertion_value.description: Expected value for the assertion (not needed for json_format).

test_cases.description: Array of test cases to run against every model.

image_base64.description: Base64-encoded image data (required unless image_url is provided).

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt sent to every VLM.

image_mime_type.description: MIME type of the image if using image_base64 (default: image/jpeg).

init_ref_tools.name: generate_eval_yaml
init_ref_tools.description: Generate a complete .ia-eval.yaml evaluation contract from a plain-language description of what your LLM should do. Uses Groq llama-3.3-70b (server-side, no API key needed). Returns ready-to-run YAML for the LLM Test Runner (run_eval_contract). Picks appropriate evaluators (cosine_similarity, contains_check, hallucination_check, etc.) based on the task type.

task_type.description: Optional task type hint to guide evaluator selection.

description.description: Plain-language description of what the LLM under test should do. Be specific: describe inputs, expected behaviour, and constraints.

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt of the LLM under test. Helps generate more accurate test cases.

scenario_count.description: Number of scenarios to generate (default: 5). Covers happy path + edge cases + adversarial.

init_ref_tools.name: generate_ci_workflow
init_ref_tools.description: Generate a ready-to-commit GitHub Actions workflow that gates a build on IA-QA. Two gate types, combinable: "eval_contract" runs a .ia-eval.yaml through ia-qa-com/eval-action@v1 (LLM quality gate, needs a provider API key as a repo secret), and "cli_checks" runs deterministic primitives via npx @ia-qa/cli (secret scan, prompt-injection scan, security headers…) whose exit code fails the build. Deterministic template — no LLM call, no API key, same inputs give the same file. Returns the YAML, the secrets to create, and the remaining steps. Pair with generate_eval_yaml to produce the contract itself.

cron.description: Cron expression when triggers include 'schedule' (default: '0 6 * * 1' — Mondays 06:00 UTC).

gate.description: Which gate to emit. eval_contract = LLM eval via the action (default). cli_checks = deterministic CLI assertions. both = CLI checks first, eval last.

provider.description: LLM provider the contract runs against — decides which repository secret the workflow wires (default: groq).

cli_tools.description: IA-QA tool names to run as deterministic gates, e.g. ["secret_scan","prompt_injection_scan"]. Tools with no known CI recipe get a --stdin step flagged in notes.

min_score.description: Override the contract min_score (0-100). Omit to use the value in the contract.

fail_on_fail.description: Fail the build on a FAIL/PARTIAL verdict (default: true). Set false to report without gating.

node_version.description: Node version for the CLI steps (default: "20").

contract_path.description: Path to the .ia-eval.yaml contract, relative to the repo root (default: evals/smoke.ia-eval.yaml). Only used when the gate includes eval_contract.

init_ref_tools.name: validate_agent_trajectory
init_ref_tools.description: Run declarative assertions on an agent trace (OpenAI tool-call messages, LangChain run trees, or plain text logs). No LLM call — deterministic. Assertion types: order (tool A before B), must_call, must_not_call, max_calls, min_calls, no_error, recovery (agent continues after error). Returns per-assertion PASS/FAIL, parsed steps, and an overall verdict. Use this to gate CI/CD on agent behavior correctness.

trace.description: Agent execution trace as JSON (OpenAI messages array, LangChain run tree) or plain text log (Thought/Action/Observation format).

tool.description: Tool name to check (for must_call, must_not_call, max_calls, min_calls).

type.description: Assertion type.

after.description: [order] Tool that must be called after.

before.description: [order] Tool that must be called first.

assertions.description: List of assertions to validate against the trace.

init_ref_tools.name: run_semantic_tests
init_ref_tools.description: Semantic assertion primitive: compare actual vs expected text pairs using cosine similarity + ROUGE-L. Two modes: tfidf (default, free, no API key) or embeddings (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, BYOK, true semantic similarity). Returns per-case PASS/FAIL verdicts and an overall verdict. CI-ready: pipe the JSON verdict field to gate a build.

mode.description: tfidf (default): fast, free, lexical. embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, true semantic similarity, requires api_key.

actual.description: The text produced by your LLM/system.

cases.description: Array of (actual, expected) pairs to evaluate.

api_key.description: OpenAI API key — required only when mode is embeddings.

require_all.description: If true (default), all cases must pass for overall PASS. If false, at least one case passing returns PASS.

init_ref_tools.name: metamorphic_check
init_ref_tools.description: Reference-free stability primitive: instead of comparing an answer to a ground truth, it checks that an assistant's answer stays INVARIANT when the QUESTION is transformed (typo, casing, paraphrase, reordering, translation). Catches the failure class no reference answer can expose — an assistant that handles one phrasing well and a trivial variant of it badly. You bring the outputs (no model is called), so it is deterministic and free in tfidf mode. Relations: case (θ .95), typo (.90), paraphrase (.80), reorder (.80), translation (.75, embeddings only), specialization (.60, ADVISORY — directional, never gated). Returns PASS / FAIL / INVALID, where INVALID means the BASE answer was a refusal or too short so invariance was never measurable — an assistant that refuses every variant would otherwise score a perfect 1.0. Use run_semantic_tests alongside it: invariance without a correctness floor is a green light for a broken assistant.

output.description: Required — the answer your system produced for the original question.

question.description: Optional — the original question, echoed back in the output for readability.

base.description: The reference run: the original question and the answer your system produced for it.

mode.description: tfidf (default): free, lexical, deterministic — but a genuine paraphrase rarely reaches 0.80, so gate on case/typo and treat paraphrase as a trend. embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, true semantic similarity, requires api_key. translation requires this mode.

api_key.description: OpenAI API key — required only when mode is embeddings.

output.description: Required — the answer your system produced for the transformed question.

question.description: Optional — the transformed question, echoed back for readability.

relation.description: Transformation applied to the QUESTION. Decides the metric and the default threshold.

variants.description: Answers produced for transformed versions of the same question, each tagged with the relation that was applied.

thresholds.description: Per-relation threshold overrides. Calibrate on your own corpus before gating — the defaults are starting points, not measurements.

require_all.description: If true (default), every gated variant must pass. If false, one passing gated variant is enough.

min_length.description: Minimum base answer length in chars (default 40).

must_not_match.description: Refusal patterns, matched case-insensitively in the FIRST 200 CHARS of the base answer (refusals lead; matching anywhere would flag a long correct answer that merely mentions one). Replaces the FR+EN default list, never merges — pass [] to disable.

baseline_guard.description: Correctness floor applied to the BASE answer before anything is scored. Failing it returns INVALID, not FAIL.

init_ref_tools.name: get_testing_guidelines
init_ref_tools.description: Query the IA-QA methodology knowledge base. Returns structured testing guidelines, assertion strategies, thresholds, best practices, and relevant MCP tools for a given topic. Call without a topic to list all available topics. Topics: llm-unit-testing, rag-pipeline, prompt-stability, prompt-ab-testing, embedding-quality, eval-framework, semantic-testing, auto-testing, security, api-testing, ci-cd, multimodal, llm-data-security, agent-observability, pro-tips, learning-paths, golden-dataset.

topic.description: The testing topic to retrieve guidelines for. Omit to get the full list of available topics.

init_ref_tools.name: test_skill
init_ref_tools.description: Validate a SKILL.md definition (Cursor / GitHub Copilot / Windsurf) by auto-generating trigger-positive and trigger-negative scenarios, running each through the model with the skill injected as a system prompt, and scoring trigger accuracy + step adherence. Returns a PASS/FIX/BLOCK verdict with per-scenario breakdown. Uses Groq llama-3.3-70b by default (server key, no api_key needed). Pass api_key + model to use your own provider.

model.description: LLM model ID to use for both scenario generation and testing (e.g. gpt-4o-mini, claude-3-5-haiku-20241022). Defaults to llama-3.3-70b-versatile (Groq, server key).

api_key.description: API key for the chosen model provider. Not required when using the default Groq model.

skill_md.description: Full content of the SKILL.md file to test. Must include a name, a "Use when:" trigger description, and at least one step.

scenario_count.description: Number of test scenarios to generate: half trigger-positive, half trigger-negative. Default: 6.

init_ref_tools.name: identify_caller
init_ref_tools.description: Returns what the server knows about the current MCP client: clientInfo captured during initialize, User-Agent, and any _meta fields sent with this request. Useful for debugging caller identification.

_meta.description: Optional self-identification. Keys: agent (string), model (string), version (string).

init_ref_tools.name: yaml_to_json
init_ref_tools.description: Parse a YAML string and return the equivalent JSON value. The reverse of json_to_yaml. Supports nested objects, arrays, anchors, aliases, multi-document streams, and all scalar types. Use when processing config files, CI/CD pipeline definitions, or OpenAPI specs authored in YAML.

multi.description: If true, parse all documents in a multi-document stream and return an array (default: false)

init_ref_tools.name: env_parse
init_ref_tools.description: Parse a .env file content into a JSON object. Handles quoted values (single and double), inline comments, export prefix, and escaped sequences (\n, \t inside double quotes). Returns all key-value pairs. Use in CI/CD pipelines, agent config loaders, or when processing dotenv files programmatically.

input.description: .env file content to parse (e.g. the output of `cat .env`)

init_ref_tools.name: json_schema_generate
init_ref_tools.description: Infer a JSON Schema (draft-07) from a sample JSON value. Detects types, required fields, array item shapes, nested objects, and common string formats (email, uri, date, date-time, uuid). Returns a ready-to-use schema compatible with json_schema_validate. Use when you have a sample API response or LLM output and want to auto-generate a validation schema for CI/CD testing.

input.description: The sample JSON value to infer the schema from — a JSON string, or the value itself.

required_all.description: Mark all detected object properties as required (default: true)

init_ref_tools.name: format_table
init_ref_tools.description: Convert a JSON array of objects into a Markdown table. Automatically detects columns, aligns headers, and fills missing keys with empty cells. Use when an agent needs to present structured data — tool results, model comparisons, test reports — as a readable table in a response or document.

input.description: The array of objects to render — a JSON string, or the array itself.

columns.description: Column names and order (default: all keys from first row)

init_ref_tools.name: openapi_validate
init_ref_tools.description: Validate the structure of an OpenAPI 3.x specification (JSON or YAML). Checks required top-level fields (openapi, info.title, info.version, paths), validates each operation (responses, operationId uniqueness), detects undeclared $ref components, and flags missing 2xx responses. Returns a PASS/FAIL verdict, a 0–100 compliance score, and a list of errors and warnings with JSON-pointer locations. Use before publishing an API spec or generating SDK code.

input.description: The OpenAPI 3.x spec — a JSON string, a YAML string, or the already-parsed spec object.

init_ref_tools.name: post_jira_comment
init_ref_tools.description: Post the output of jira_to_test_suite as a formatted comment on the source Jira ticket. Converts Gherkin, E2E steps, API tests, and ambiguities into Atlassian Document Format (ADF). STATEFUL — creates a comment on the issue.

test_suite.description: The test_suite object from jira_to_test_suite result

init_ref_tools.name: create_confluence_page
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new Confluence page from the output of jira_to_test_suite. Formats Gherkin, E2E steps, API tests, and test data as a properly structured Confluence page with code blocks and tables. STATEFUL — creates a new page in the specified space.

issue_key.description: Source Jira issue key (for the page title and source link)

issue_url.description: Source Jira issue URL (added as a link in the page)

space_key.description: Confluence space key where the page will be created, e.g. "QA", "ENG"

test_suite.description: The test_suite object from jira_to_test_suite result

parent_page_id.description: Optional parent page ID — page will be created as a child of this page

init_ref_tools.name: fetch_jira_issue
init_ref_tools.description: Fetch a complete Jira issue: summary, description converted to Markdown, status, assignee, priority, labels, custom fields, and optionally comments and attachment metadata. BYOK — credentials transit in-memory only, never stored on ia-qa.com.

fields.description: Specific Jira field names to return. Omit for all standard fields.

jira_token.description: Atlassian API token (from id.atlassian.com > Security > API tokens)

include_comments.description: Include issue comments, up to 20 (default: true)

init_ref_tools.name: search_jira_issues
init_ref_tools.description: Search Jira using JQL (Jira Query Language). Returns matching issues with key fields. Ideal for finding open bugs, sprint tickets, or issues by label/assignee/component. BYOK — credentials transit in-memory only, never stored.

jql.description: JQL query string, e.g. "project = PROJ AND status = Open AND assignee = currentUser() ORDER BY priority DESC"

fields.description: Fields per issue. Default: summary, status, assignee, priority, issuetype, labels, created, updated

init_ref_tools.name: jira_to_test_suite
init_ref_tools.description: Transform a Jira ticket into a complete test suite: Gherkin scenarios, E2E steps, API test cases, test data matrix, and ambiguity detection. Accepts either Jira credentials (auto-fetch) or a pre-fetched issue object. The returned test_suite includes _gherkin_warnings (deterministic syntax validation — empty if clean). Requires BYOK LLM key (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.).

issue.description: Pre-fetched issue object from fetch_jira_issue, OR a mock object with fields: key, summary, description (plain text or Markdown), status, issue_type, priority, labels, comments. Use this for offline/CI testing without Jira credentials.

model.description: LLM model to use, e.g. "gpt-4o-mini", "claude-3-5-haiku-20241022", "gemini-2.0-flash".

api_key.description: Your LLM provider API key (OpenAI sk-, Anthropic sk-ant-, Google AIzaSy-, etc.).

issue_key.description: Jira issue key to fetch automatically, e.g. "PROJ-123". Required if issue is not provided.

jira_email.description: Atlassian account email. Required for auto-fetch mode.

jira_token.description: Atlassian API token. Required for auto-fetch mode.

max_tokens.description: Maximum tokens for the LLM response. Default: 8192. Increase for large tickets with many ACs; decrease to reduce cost on simple tickets.

jira_base_url.description: Atlassian base URL. Required for auto-fetch mode.

confluence_pages.description: Optional array of pre-fetched Confluence page objects from fetch_confluence_page, used as documentation context.

init_ref_tools.name: fix_gherkin
init_ref_tools.description: Fix Gherkin syntax warnings from a jira_to_test_suite result. Takes the current gherkin text and the _gherkin_warnings array, calls your LLM to fix ONLY the flagged issues (adds missing Given/When/Then steps, etc.), and returns the corrected Gherkin. Lightweight — uses ~300-500 tokens vs ~5k for a full regeneration. Requires BYOK LLM key.

model.description: LLM model to use for the fix, e.g. "gpt-4o-mini". Must belong to the provider whose key you passed in api_key.

api_key.description: Your own LLM provider API key (BYOK) — OpenAI "sk-…", Anthropic "sk-ant-…", Google "AIzaSy…", or Groq "gsk_…". There is no server-side key for this tool: if you do not have one, do not call it and do not invent a value — placeholders like "configured", "your_api_key" or a masked "sk-…***…" are rejected. Used for this call only, never stored.

gherkin.description: The current Gherkin text from the jira_to_test_suite result (test_suite.gherkin).

warnings.description: The _gherkin_warnings array from the jira_to_test_suite result.

init_ref_tools.name: fetch_confluence_page
init_ref_tools.description: Fetch a Confluence page and return its content as clean Markdown. Accepts a numeric page_id or a full page URL. Optionally lists direct child pages. BYOK — credentials transit in-memory only, never stored.

page_url.description: Full Confluence page URL (alternative to page_id), e.g. "https://mycompany.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123456789"

confluence_email.description: Atlassian account email (same credentials as Jira)

include_children.description: List direct child pages (id + title) (default: false)

init_ref_tools.name: rate_tool
init_ref_tools.description: Give honest usage feedback on an IA-QA MCP tool. Provide a score (1-5) and a comment. Rate low (1-2) if the tool was wrong, irrelevant, or a poor fit; rate high (4-5) only if it genuinely solved your need. Ratings are aggregated on a public dashboard at /devtools/mcp-ratings. Skip rating routine successes — we want signal, not praise. Example: rate_tool({ tool_name: "format_json", score: 2, comment: "Tried to pretty-print a JSON5 file, it rejected trailing commas — not usable for my case." })

comment.description: Strongly encouraged — explain what you were trying to do and whether the tool got you there. Be specific about what was missing, wrong, or a poor fit. This is the most valuable part of the rating. Up to 2000 chars are stored; go over and the response says so (truncated: true) — send the remainder as a second call rather than assuming it landed.

tool_name.description: Name of the MCP tool to rate (e.g. "format_json", "shield_analyze")

source_metadata.display_name: ia-qa.com/mcp llm and RAG testing - Dev/QA toolbox

environment.description: Read Slack conversations, threads, and user directories, send messages, and invite users to channels.

init_ref_tools.name: Arcade_ListApps
init_ref_tools.description: See the apps the current caller can act on and whether they are connected. Returns each app's id, name, connected state, and (when connected) the account it is connected as. Call this to answer "what apps do I have?" or when the caller's connection state may have changed since the session started.

init_ref_tools.name: Slack_GetConversationMetadata
init_ref_tools.description:
Get metadata of a Channel, a Direct Message (IM / DM) or a Multi-Person (MPIM) conversation.

Use this tool to retrieve metadata about a conversation with a conversation_id, a channel name,
or by the user_id(s), username(s), and/or email(s) of the user(s) in the conversation.

This tool does not return the messages in a conversation. To get the messages, use the
'Slack.GetMessages' tool instead.

Provide exactly one of:
- conversation_id; or
- channel_name; or
- any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

emails.description: The emails of the users to get the conversation metadata.

user_ids.description: The IDs of the users to get the conversation metadata.

usernames.description: The usernames of the users to get the conversation metadata. Prefer providing user_ids and/or emails, when available, since the performance is better.

channel_name.description: The name of the channel to get metadata for. Prefer providing a conversation_id, when available, since the performance is better.

conversation_id.description: The ID of the conversation to get metadata for

init_ref_tools.name: Slack_GetMessages
init_ref_tools.description:
Get messages in a Slack Channel, DM (direct message) or MPIM (multi-person) conversation.

Provide exactly one of:
- conversation_id; or
- channel_name; or
- any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

To filter messages by an absolute datetime, use 'oldest_datetime' and/or 'latest_datetime'. If
only 'oldest_datetime' is provided, it will return messages from the oldest_datetime to the
current time. If only 'latest_datetime' is provided, it will return messages since the
beginning of the conversation to the latest_datetime.

To filter messages by a relative datetime, use 'oldest_relative' and/or 'latest_relative'
with numeric `DD:HH:MM` offsets only. Convert relative phrases to `DD:HH:MM` before calling
this tool. If only 'oldest_relative' is provided, it will return messages from the
oldest_relative to the current time. If only 'latest_relative' is provided, it will return
messages from the current time to the latest_relative.

Do not provide both 'oldest_datetime' and 'oldest_relative' or both 'latest_datetime' and
'latest_relative'.

Leave all arguments with the default None to get messages without date/time filtering

limit.description: The maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 20. Maximum is 100.

emails.description: The emails of the users in the conversation to get messages from.

user_ids.description: The IDs of the users in the conversation to get messages from.

usernames.description: The usernames of the users in the conversation to get messages from. Prefer providinguser_ids and/or emails, when available, since the performance is better.

next_cursor.description: The cursor to use for pagination.

channel_name.description: The name of the channel to get messages from. Prefer providing a conversation_id, when available, since the performance is better.

conversation_id.description: The ID of the conversation to get messages from. Provide exactly one of conversation_id OR any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

latest_datetime.description: The latest message to include in the results, specified as a datetime object in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' or ISO 8601.

latest_relative.description: The latest message to include in the results, specified as a time offset from the current time. Use only the numeric 'DD:HH:MM' format; convert relative phrases to that format before calling this tool.

oldest_datetime.description: The oldest message to include in the results, specified as a datetime object in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' or ISO 8601.

oldest_relative.description: The oldest message to include in the results, specified as a time offset from the current time. Use only the numeric 'DD:HH:MM' format; convert relative phrases to that format before calling this tool.

init_ref_tools.name: Slack_GetThreadMessages
init_ref_tools.description:
Get messages in a Slack thread.

A thread is a collection of messages grouped together as replies to a parent message.
This tool retrieves all messages in a specific thread, identified by the parent message's
timestamp (thread_ts).

Provide exactly one of:
- conversation_id; or
- channel_name; or
- any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

To filter messages by an absolute datetime, use 'oldest_datetime' and/or 'latest_datetime'. If
only 'oldest_datetime' is provided, it will return messages from the oldest_datetime to the
current time. If only 'latest_datetime' is provided, it will return messages since the
beginning of the thread to the latest_datetime.

To filter messages by a relative datetime, use 'oldest_relative' and/or 'latest_relative'
with numeric `DD:HH:MM` offsets only. Convert relative phrases to `DD:HH:MM` before calling
this tool. If only 'oldest_relative' is provided, it will return messages from the
oldest_relative to the current time. If only 'latest_relative' is provided, it will return
messages from the current time to the latest_relative.

Do not provide both 'oldest_datetime' and 'oldest_relative' or both 'latest_datetime' and
'latest_relative'.

Leave all datetime arguments with the default None to get all thread messages without
date/time filtering.

limit.description: The maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 20. Maximum is 100.

emails.description: The emails of the users in the conversation containing the thread.

user_ids.description: The IDs of the users in the conversation containing the thread.

thread_ts.description: The timestamp of the parent message that starts the thread. This is the 'ts' field from the parent message.

usernames.description: The usernames of the users in the conversation containing the thread. Prefer providing user_ids and/or emails, when available, since the performance is better.

next_cursor.description: The cursor to use for pagination.

channel_name.description: The name of the channel containing the thread. Prefer providing a conversation_id, when available, since the performance is better.

conversation_id.description: The ID of the conversation containing the thread. Provide exactly one of conversation_id OR channel_name OR any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

latest_datetime.description: The latest message to include in the results, specified as a datetime object in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' or ISO 8601.

latest_relative.description: The latest message to include in the results, specified as a time offset from the current time. Use only the numeric 'DD:HH:MM' format; convert relative phrases to that format before calling this tool.

oldest_datetime.description: The oldest message to include in the results, specified as a datetime object in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' or ISO 8601.

oldest_relative.description: The oldest message to include in the results, specified as a time offset from the current time. Use only the numeric 'DD:HH:MM' format; convert relative phrases to that format before calling this tool.

init_ref_tools.name: Slack_GetUsersInConversation
init_ref_tools.description:
Get the users in a Slack conversation (Channel, DM/IM, or MPIM) by its ID or by channel name.

Provide exactly one of conversation_id or channel_name. Prefer providing a conversation_id,
when available, since the performance is better.

limit.description: The maximum number of users to return. Defaults to 200. Maximum is 500.

next_cursor.description: The cursor to use for pagination.

Provide any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails. If you need to retrieve
data about multiple users, DO NOT CALL THE TOOL MULTIPLE TIMES. Instead, call it once
with all the user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

If you need to get metadata or messages of a conversation, use the
`Slack.GetConversationMetadata` or `Slack.GetMessages` tool instead. These
tools accept user_ids, usernames, and/or emails. Do not retrieve users' info first,
as it is inefficient.

emails.description: The emails of the users to get

user_ids.description: The IDs of the users to get

usernames.description: The usernames of the users to get. Prefer retrieving by user_ids and/or emails, when available, since the performance is better.

init_ref_tools.name: Slack_InviteUsersToChannel
init_ref_tools.description:
Invite users to a Slack channel or MPIM (multi-person direct message).

This tool invites specified users to join a Slack conversation. It works with:
- Public channels
- Private channels
- MPIMs (multi-person direct messages / group DMs)

You can specify users by their user IDs, usernames, or email addresses.

Provide exactly one of channel_id or channel_name, and at least one of user_ids, usernames,
or emails.

The tool will resolve usernames and emails to user IDs before inviting them.
Up to 100 users may be invited at once.

emails.description: The email addresses of the people to invite.

user_ids.description: The Slack user IDs of the people to invite. Up to 100 users may be listed. Provide at least one of user_ids, usernames, or emails.

usernames.description: The Slack usernames of the people to invite. Prefer providing user_ids and/or emails when available for better performance.

channel_name.description: The name of the channel to invite users to. Prefer providing a channel_id when available for better performance. Note: MPIMs don't have names, so use channel_id for MPIMs.

init_ref_tools.description:
List metadata for Slack conversations (channels, DMs, MPIMs) the user is a member of.

This tool does not return the messages in a conversation. To get the messages, use the

init_ref_tools.name: Slack_ListUsers

List all users in the authenticated user's Slack team.

If you need to get metadata or messages of a conversation, use the
`Slack.GetConversationMetadata` tool or `Slack.GetMessages` tool instead. These
tools accept a user_id, username, and/or email. Do not use this tool to first retrieve user(s),
as it is inefficient.

init_ref_tools.name: Slack_SendMessage
init_ref_tools.description:
Send a message to a Channel, Direct Message (IM/DM), or Multi-Person (MPIM) conversation.

Can send top-level messages or reply to an existing thread.

Provide exactly one of:
- channel_name; or
- conversation_id; or
- any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

In case multiple user_ids, usernames, and/or emails are provided, the tool will open a
multi-person conversation with the specified people and send the message to it.

To reply to a thread, also provide thread_ts (the 'ts' field of the parent message).
Optionally set reply_broadcast to true to also post the reply to the main conversation.

emails.description: The emails of the people to message.

message.description: The content of the message to send.

user_ids.description: The Slack user IDs of the people to message.

thread_ts.description: The timestamp of the parent message to reply to in a thread. Use the 'ts' field from the parent message (the first message in the thread), not from a reply. If omitted, the message is sent as a new top-level message. Get this value from prior get_messages or get_thread_messages results.

usernames.description: The Slack usernames of the people to message. Prefer providing user_ids and/or emails, when available, since the performance is better.

channel_name.description: The channel name to send the message to. Prefer providing a conversation_id, when available, since the performance is better.

conversation_id.description: The conversation ID to send the message to.

reply_broadcast.description: When replying to a thread (thread_ts is set), set to true to also post the reply to the main conversation. Only valid when thread_ts is provided. Defaults to False

init_ref_tools.name: Slack_WhoAmI
init_ref_tools.description:
Get comprehensive user profile and Slack information.

This tool provides detailed information about the authenticated user including
their name, email, profile picture, and other important profile details from
Slack services.

environment.description:
Create long-form (faceless YouTube) videos end to end from any MCP client: script, locked character references, storyboard, voiceover, and final video editing — with characters and style held consistent across every shot.

Making long-form AI video today means 8+ tabs stitched by hand — an LLM for the script, a voice model, an image model, a video model — with characters drifting between tools and style resetting at every export. Framesail replaces the patchwork: the whole pipeline runs in one place and manages your video's context end to end.

Six stages: Style (paste images, videos, or YouTube links and Framesail reverse-engineers the look, voice, and direction), Script (write it yourself or generate it in your narrative style), Reference images (auto-generated for every character, place, and prop), Voiceover (one narrator or many characters, with word-level timing), Storyboard (planned scene by scene), and Editor (captions, music, SFX, then export).

No black box: you control every prompt, asset, model, and setting.
